item.title: Customs to strictly examine import consignments
item.description:
Customs intelligence units are asked to coordinate examinations of import consignments to avert cumbersome crosscheck and thus reduce port clearance time and cost of business for importers.
The National Board of Revenue (NBR) has issued the order for customs intelligence units to coordinate with the Customs Intelligence and Investigation Directorate (CIID) and the Central Intelligence Cell (CIC) in such work, as businesses often resent overlapping of trade scrutiny.
Customs officials have also been instructed not to seek documents beyond those specified in the Goods Declaration, Assessment and Re-assessment Rules 2024.
They cannot demand manual copies of documents already submitted electronically.
The directives are part of 12 urgent instructions issued by the NBR to customs houses and stations across Bangladesh to ensure revenue security while expediting the clearance of imported goods.
It was a long-pressed demand from the business community to simplify customs process and coordinate investigation processes rather than separately seeking documents from them.
The government's revenue authority has also instructed customs authorities to strengthen risk-based examination, eliminate unnecessary procedures and avoid multiple physical examinations of the same consignment unless a confirmed risk does exist.
The directions on dos and don'ts, issued on August 30, call for regular updating of the Asycuda World System selectivity criteria so that consignments can be selected for examination based on revenue risks.
"Findings from physical examinations should also be used to improve future risk-selection criteria," said the latest order on external-trade front.
The NBR has also directed officials to avoid unnecessary manual registers and data recording and not to forward files of non-risky consignments to higher authorities unless there are specific instructions from the revenue board.
Responsible officers must regularly monitor unstuffing activities and gate verification at sea, land and air ports, it said.
All unnecessary steps in the assessment and clearance process should be eliminated, according to the directives.
To expedite the release of imported goods, customs authorities have been asked to issue notices to importers and clearing and forwarding (C&F) agents and take legal action where necessary.
The NBR has also ordered customs authorities to complete auction procedures for stuck-up goods swiftly.
The notification, signed by Second Secretary (Customs: Policy) Rezaul Karim, was circulated to major Customs, Excise and VAT Commissionerates for immediate implementation.

item.title: Savings tools: Premature encashment cuts profit; lack of TIN increases tax
item.description:
When thinking of safe investments, National Savings Certificates ( Sanchayapatra ) are the top choice for many.
For middle-income and fixed-income individuals in particular, it serves as both a means of saving and a source of regular income.
Many also invest with future needs in mind, such as education, medical treatment, or household emergencies.
However, without a clear understanding of maturity periods, profit rules, taxation, and personal financial needs prior to purchasing, investors may fail to earn desired returns—or even face financial losses when attempting to withdraw funds during emergencies.
Five mistakes to avoid before buying savings certificates
It is unwise to invest funds into long-term savings certificates if they might be needed soon for emergency funds, medical care, or urgent expenses. Capital is generally locked in for several years. Breaking certificates before maturity means forfeiting expected profit rates. If there is a chance you will need the money within a few months, it is best not to invest those funds in savings certificates.
Profit rates and governing rules vary depending on the total investment amount. Before committing large sums, it is essential to verify current rules, overall investment limits, and applicable profit tiers. If planning to invest under the names of multiple family members, consider the source of funds, legal ownership, and tax regulations separately for each individual. Investments should never be made in someone else’s name solely to evade taxes.
Withholding tax applies to profits earned from savings certificates. Lacking proper clarity on Tax Identification Numbers (TIN), tax return filings, and related tax rules may lead to higher tax deductions from your profit than expected. Before purchasing, it is advisable to check your tax status and applicable withholding tax rates with relevant authorities or a tax professional.
Not all savings certificate schemes distribute profits in the same manner. Some investors require regular monthly income, while others prefer receiving a lump sum upon maturity. For instance, Family Savings Certificates offer regular profit payouts, while others pay out quarterly. Rather than looking solely at the highest profit rate, select a scheme based on your specific financial needs and cash flow requirements.
Putting all future savings exclusively into savings certificates is not a risk-free strategy. It is far better to create separate plans for short-, medium-, and long-term horizons aligned with your financial needs. Alongside setting aside easily accessible funds for emergency expenses, plan for long-term investments. This reduces the risk of having to break long-term investments prematurely when sudden cash needs arise.
Before buying savings certificates
Before investing, it is essential to learn about the current profit rates, tenure, investment limits, tax rules, and early encashment penalties for the specific savings certificate.
Additionally, decisions should be made taking into account your personal financial goals and future cash flow requirements.
Rather than investing all savings into a single sector simply because it feels safe, investing based on a comprehensive financial plan is far more important.
Investment Scenario / Factor
Key Risk / Impact
Recommended Strategy
Premature Encashment
Reduced Profit Yield: Breaking certificates before maturity forfeits standard yields; profits are recalculated at lower penalty rates.
Keep emergency reserves in liquid bank accounts; only lock funds intended for full tenure.
Missing TIN / Tax Return
Higher Tax Deduction: Higher withholding tax rates are levied on profit distributions if TIN/tax return proof is not updated.
Obtain a valid TIN and file annual income tax returns to qualify for lower withholding tax rates.
Exceeding Investment Slabs
Lower Effective Returns: Crossing specific investment thresholds (slabs) drops the applicable profit rate tier.
Review individual and joint holding limits across all schemes prior to purchasing.
Mismatched Payout Structure
Cash Flow Distress: Choosing maturity-based growth schemes when regular cash is required causes liquidity strains.
Align scheme choice (e.g., Family Savings Certificate for monthly payouts vs. 3-Month Profit Certificate) with cash flow needs.
Single-Asset Allocation
Liquidity Lockup: Concentrating 100% of wealth into long-term certificates leaves no buffer for unexpected costs.
Diversify into a mix of short-term liquid funds, medium-term deposits, and long-term certificates.
Government savings certificates in Bangladesh offer tiered returns where maximum yields are unlocked only upon reaching full maturity (e.g., 3 or 5 years).
Encashment within the first year often yields minimal to zero profit, while early withdrawal in subsequent years slashes the rate retroactively.
Having a Tax Identification Number (TIN) and filing proof of income tax returns directly protects your investment yield by preventing maximum source tax deductions (e.g., reducing withholding tax rates from higher penalty brackets down to standard rates).

item.description:
Japanese automakers Nissan and Honda have agreed to jointly develop computer components and software for vehicles expected to enter the market in fiscal 2029, the companies said Monday.
Under the agreement, Yokohama-based Nissan and Tokyo-based Honda will share standardized components for core electronic control units, or ECUs, as well as software.
The two companies began discussions in 2024 on cooperation in electric vehicles and automotive intelligence technology. Their latest agreement focuses on software-defined vehicles, whose functions and features can be controlled and updated through software rather than hardware. The announcement did not mention specific vehicle models or electric vehicles.
The global auto industry is increasingly shifting toward technologies such as automated driving, electrification and zero-emission vehicles, making cars more dependent on electronic systems and software.
The companies said sharing components and jointly conducting research could reduce costs, speed up development and create greater efficiency through large-scale production.
European automakers Volkswagen, BMW, Mercedes-Benz and Stellantis are also cooperating on software development and shared operating systems.
Nissan and Honda, both smaller than industry leader Toyota Motor Corp. in Japan, believe closer cooperation could strengthen their competitiveness.
The companies said they would also explore cooperation in areas including zero-emission technology and reducing traffic deaths.
Both stressed that faster development, efficient investment, electrification and intelligent vehicle technology would remain key priorities of their strategic partnership.

item.description:
A Dhaka court on Monday sent two leaders of the BNP and its student wing, Chhatra Dal, to jail in a case filed over the snatching of gold jewelry in Dhaka airport area.
The court also fixed Tuesday for hearing their bail petitions.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Hasan Shahadat passed the order after the accused were produced before the court following a one-day remand. Abu Bakkar, a sub-inspector of the Prosecution Department, confirmed the matter.
The accused are Al-Amin Hasan Shanto, general secretary of the Airport Thana unit of Chhatra Dal, and Md Abdur Rouf, president of the Airport unit of BNP.
Kamrul Hasan, officer-in-charge of Airport Police Station, told Dhaka Tribune that the two were produced before the court on Monday after completing their one-day remand.
The court had earlier granted police one day’s remand for each of them after investigators sought three days to question them.
The incident took place on the night of August 28 in front of Balaka Bhaban on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway in the Airport area.
On August 29, Md Sumon filed a case with Airport Police Station over the incident.
Police later analyzed CCTV footage and conducted an operation to arrest people allegedly involved in the incident.
On August 30, investigating officer Sub-Inspector Sabbir Hossain produced the accused before the court and sought three days’ remand. The court granted one day’s remand for each.
After the remand period ended, the investigating officer sought an order to keep the accused in jail.
In the application, the investigating officer said the accused had provided information about the incident during interrogation, which was still being verified.
The application also said there was a strong possibility that the accused could go into hiding and hamper the investigation if released on bail.
The investigating officer therefore sought their detention in jail in the interest of a proper investigation and justice.
At Monday’s hearing, defense lawyer Abdul Rahman sought time for the bail petitions to be heard on Tuesday. The court subsequently sent the accused to jail and fixed Tuesday for the bail hearing.
According to the First Information Report (FIR), the complainant said his elder brother, Kawsar, is an expatriate living in Malaysia.
On August 28, Kawsar sent 200 grams of gold jewelry from Malaysia for his sister’s wedding and family use.
Later that evening, around 8pm, the complainant and his friend Rohan Chowdhury collected the jewelry from an acquaintance of Kawsar at the airport.
They then traveled in a rented microbus and got off opposite Balaka Bhaban on the Dhaka-Mymensingh Highway.
The FIR says the accused allegedly surrounded them as soon as they got out of the microbus and beat them after accusing them of being involved in Awami League and Chhatra League politics.
The accused also allegedly claimed that the two were carrying bombs.
At one point, the accused allegedly snatched the 200 grams of gold jewelry and fled the scene.
The FIR says the accused quickly left the area as people began gathering at the scene.
The FIR names four people as accused: Abdur Rouf, 40, president of the Airport unit of BNP; Ripon, 27, president of the Airport Thana unit of JCD; Al-Amin Shanto, 27, general secretary of the Airport Thana unit of JCD; and Rubel, 32, general secretary of an Airport ward unit of BNP.

item.title: Civil aviation minister: Bangladesh buying 14 Boeing aircraft, plans to lease more
item.description:
Civil Aviation and Tourism Minister M Rashiduzzaman Millat on Monday said Bangladesh is buying 14 Boeing aircraft from the United States and it has also plans to lease some additional aircraft.
“The US had requested that Bangladesh use Boeing aircraft, and the government is acting accordingly,” he told reporters, responding to a question over the government’s reported plan to purchase Boeing aircraft from the United States.
The minister attended a law-and-order and development coordination meeting as the chief guest at the conference room of the Mymensingh deputy commissioner in the afternoon.
Millat said Bangladesh will procure new aircraft from Airbus, jointly manufactured by France, Britain and Germany, as part of efforts to modernise and strengthen the aviation sector.
U.S. Special Envoy for South and Central Asia and its Ambassador to India Sergio Gor has said Bangladesh has committed billions of dollars to buy additional Boeing aircraft from the United States under a new deal between Dhaka and Washington.
In April, Bangladesh signed a deal with US aircraft manufacturer Boeing to buy 14 planes for its national carrier Biman Bangladesh Airlines, the two sides announced - the airline’s biggest-ever order, in a deal valued at $3.7 billion.
The government is working round the clock to resolve the existing problems in the country’s power and energy sectors, describing the current electricity and gas crisis as a “mess” left by its predecessors.
He said a sustainable solution to the crisis would take time and strict action would be taken against those seeking to create disorder and administrative instability.
“Gas and electricity during Sheikh Hasina’s time have left us in trouble. But we are carrying this trouble; we did not create it,” he said.
Responding to criticism over the electricity and gas shortages, the minister said some opposition lawmakers and representatives of Jamaat-e-Islami frequently stage movements demanding the government step down for failing to ensure adequate power and gas supplies.
“But if you ask us to step down, can you provide electricity tomorrow? Can you provide electricity or gas within six months? You cannot,” he said.
Millat said resolving the crisis and developing new infrastructure would require time.
“Even after laying the foundation stone of a building, it takes at least two years to complete it. Even if we work rapidly using new technologies, it will still take one-and-a-half to two years,” he said.
“We are working day and night toward that goal,” he added.
The minister also urged law-enforcement agencies and administration officials to take strict measures against those attempting to create social and administrative instability.
“We must not create disorder at every turn. Those who want to create social and administrative instability must be dealt with firmly,” he said, instructing officials to properly enforce existing laws.
“Our only goal is to ensure that people live in peace and get a better Bangladesh,” he said.
Senior officials of the local administration, lawmakers, representatives of law-enforcement agencies and officials from different government departments were also present.

item.title: Teacher’s death in snatching: Three placed on remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Monday placed three men on five-day remand each in a case filed over the death of primary school headteacher Ranjila Parveen, 56, who fell from an autorickshaw after snatchers grabbed her bag near the south plaza of the National Parliament.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Md Siddique Azad passed the order following a petition by the investigating officer.
The accused are Poni, alias Para Poni, alias Poni Gazi; Cedric Julian; and Rakib Hossain.
Sub-Inspector Shahin of Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station, also the investigating officer in the case, produced the three accused before the court and sought a 10-day remand.
Lawyers Amir Uddin Amir and Shahadat Hossain Mamun, representing the accused, sought bail and urged the court to reject the remand plea.
During the hearing, the defense lawyers said the accused were not connected to the incident and urged the court to ensure that the actual perpetrators were brought to justice.
“We want the real culprits to be tried. No innocent person should be harassed,” they said.
They also claimed that the motorcycle identified in connection with the case did not match the one used to arrest the accused and alleged that the case was being diverted in another direction.
The court, however, granted five days’ remand for each of the accused.
Speaking to reporters after the hearing, Poni denied any involvement in the incident.
“We are not connected to this incident. The truth will prevail. RAB is fake. AI cameras are everywhere now, so we are not afraid. Allah will do something about this,” he said.
RAB-2 arrested the three men during an operation on Sunday and seized a Yamaha R15 motorcycle allegedly used in the snatching.
According to the case statement, Parveen was the headteacher of Bagbari Government Primary School in Gabtoli upazila of Bogra.
At around 5:55am on August 29, she was traveling by auto-rickshaw with her husband, Md Abdul Matin, to see an eye doctor.
When they were on the paved road near Gate 12 of the National Parliament on Manik Mia Avenue, snatchers riding a motorcycle grabbed her bag and pulled it forcefully.
The force of the pull caused Parveen to fall from the moving auto-rickshaw onto the paved road, leaving her with a severe head injury.
She was taken in critical condition to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital and later to Dhaka Medical College Hospital, but doctors declared her dead on the way.
Her husband filed the case at Sher-e-Bangla Nagar police station on Sunday.

item.title: Rangpur murders: Dope tests of two accused negative
item.description:
The dope test reports of two accused in the Rangpur four-murder case have come back negative, with no evidence of drug use found in their blood or urine samples.
Rangpur Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) Deputy Commissioner Sanatan Chakraborty confirmed the matter on Monday afternoon, saying no signs of drug use were detected.
The samples of accused Mugdha Das and Siddharth Das, who are currently in Rangpur Central Jail, were collected on Sunday after the court approved a request for their dope tests.
Investigating DB police Officer-in-Charge Jinnat Ali said the accused were not taken out of the prison for security reasons. Instead, technologists from Rangpur Medical College were brought to the jail to collect their blood and urine samples.
Rangpur Medical College technologist Mohammad Ashraf said urine samples were collected from the two accused for testing.
Sanatan Chakraborty, also the spokesperson for Rangpur Metropolitan Police, said the case was highly sensitive and there was a risk of attacks or mob gatherings if the accused were taken outside the prison.
He said the tests conducted at the Rangpur Medical College laboratory found no evidence of drug use and the reports were subsequently submitted as negative.
Sanatan Chakraborty declined to comment further on the reports.
The negative dope tests have raised questions about the police’s earlier account of the motive behind the killings.
Police had said the accused, Siddharth and Mugdha Das, consumed four yaba tablets at their friend Simanta Das’s house before going to the home of retired schoolteacher Ganapati Chakraborty.
According to the police account, they later went to the house of alleged drug dealer Shanto and bought four more yaba tablets by pawning their mobile phones. They then climbed onto the roof of a neighbouring house and entered Ganapati’s roof, where they allegedly consumed yaba.
Police said Ganapati saw them, shouted and threatened them, after which the accused allegedly killed him and three members of his family.
The police’s account has come under renewed scrutiny following the negative dope test results.
On the night of August 22, police recovered the bodies of Ganapati Chakraborty, his wife, daughter and son from a locked house in the Masuapara, also known as Daspara, area of Rangpur city.
Neighbours Mugdha Das and Siddharth Das were subsequently arrested in connection with the killings.
Ganapati’s elder brother Gopinath Chakraborty filed a murder case with Kotwali police station.
The two accused later gave confessional statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure before a court.
The case is currently being investigated by the police’s Detective Branch.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 973 as six die in 24 hours
item.description:
Six more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Monday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 973.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all six of the latest casualties as suspected.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 874, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 99, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
Among the six new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with five deaths reported in the Dhaka division and four in Dhaka district.
A total of 1,162 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Monday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 157,991.
During the same period, 94 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 19,312.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 138,445 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 133,404 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: High Court upholds death sentence in Magura child rape-murder case
item.description:
The High Court has upheld the death sentence of Hitu Sheikh in the widely discussed rape and murder case of an eight-year-old child in Magura.
A High Court bench comprising Justice Bhishmadev Chakraborty and Justice KM Rasheduzzaman Raja began announcing the verdict at 11am on Monday.
The verdict was initially scheduled for August 25 but was deferred after the state sought more time.
State-appointed lawyer Hafizur Rahman Khan represented Hitu Sheikh, while Deputy Attorney General Imam Hasan Tarek appeared for the state, assisted by Assistant Attorney General Rohani Siddique and Mahbuba Tasnim Ankhi.
The hearing on the death reference and appeal began on August 11.
In early March 2025, the child was allegedly raped and sexually assaulted while visiting her sister's in-laws in Nijnanduali village of Magura. She was initially taken to hospitals in Magura and Faridpur in critical condition. As her condition deteriorated, she was transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital and later to Combined Military Hospital, where she died on March 13.
On May 17, 2025, Magura Women and Children Repression Prevention Tribunal Judge M Zahid Hasan sentenced the main accused, the father-in-law of the child's sister, to death. The court acquitted the other three accused.
The case documents were subsequently sent to the High Court as a death reference.
Amid several incidents of violence against women and children, Chief Justice Zubair Rahman Chowdhury formed a special High Court bench on June 10, 2026, to prioritise death references and appeals in cases under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act.
A special team of state lawyers was also formed to assist the bench. Led by Attorney General Barrister Md Ruhul Quddus Kazal, the team includes deputy attorney generals Mohammad Imam Hossain Tarek and Syed Ejaz Kabir, and assistant attorney generals Mahbuba Tasnim Ankhi, Mustafizur Rahman Mukul, Ashraful Alam, Rohani Siddique and Al Amin Siddique.

item.title: Asif Mahmud: NCP views Makkah Pact positively
item.description:
National Citizens Party (NCP) spokesperson Asif Mahmud Shojib Bhuyain has said the party views the Makkah Pact positively, while its subcommittee is closely monitoring the issue.
He made the remarks at a press conference at the airport on Monday morning after returning home from performing Umrah.
The Makkah Pact, also known as the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement, is a trilateral defence agreement between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey.
Asif Mahmud also alleged that a syndicate linked to the ruling BNP had become active again, saying airfares to Saudi Arabia had fallen during the interim government but increased after the BNP came to power.
He also referred to the ongoing gas and electricity crises, alleging that prices and extortion had increased across sectors since the election.
“The people are in a state of despair,” he said, urging the government to take swift measures to address the situation.

item.title: Makkah Pact: FM says no reason for anyone to be upset or worried
item.description:
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman on Sunday reiterated that the "Makkah Pact" is an internal matter of the world Muslim family and that there is no reason for anyone to be upset or worried about this.
“This is not a matter of threatening. This is not a matter of attacking anyone. This is a matter of self-defense of our world Muslim family. So I do not see any reason for anyone to be upset or worried about this,” he said.
Dr Khalilur left Dhaka on Sunday night for New York to take up his responsibilities as president of the 81st Session of the United Nations General Assembly, a tenure that will coincide with a crucial period for the world body, including the selection of a new UN secretary-general.
The foreign minister left Dhaka shortly after 8:20pm on an official visit to New York, US, in connection with his UNGA presidency from August 31 to October 21 and is scheduled to transit through Dubai, a senior official told UNB.
Asked about possible challenges in discharging the two responsibilities, Dr Khalilur said diplomats deal with realities rather than hypothetical situations.
“Look, we are diplomats. We do not work on ‘ifs’. We work on reality,” he told private television channel "Independent TV" in an interview before leaving Dhaka for New York.
The 81st session of the General Assembly will formally open on September 8, with world leaders expected to gather at UN Headquarters in New York later in the month for the annual high-level general debate.
The foreign minister said Bangladesh will maintain good relations with all countries while firmly protecting its national interests, reiterating that the government’s foreign policy is guided by the principle of “Bangladesh First.”
“Bangladesh First” means that Bangladesh is not alone. It means that we will maintain our relations by ensuring our mutual interests,” he said.
Dr Khalilur, who is set to serve as president of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, said he does not anticipate any major difficulty in handling the two responsibilities simultaneously.
He said another state minister has been appointed to the Foreign Ministry and that he has worked closely with the minister.
“So I do not see any particular challenge in performing my duties,” he said.
Dr Khalilur said the Rohingya crisis and the broader issue of refugees and displaced people would be among his priorities as President of the UN General Assembly.
“Refugees, displaced people, these are part of my priorities. I said that during my election. So I will definitely have a strong eye on this,” he said.
The issue would receive special attention during the UN General Assembly’s High-Level Week beginning September 22.
“There will be a high-level side event and I will present my statement there as President of the General Assembly,” he said.
Dr Khalilur reiterated Bangladesh’s longstanding position that repatriation is the only sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis.
“There is only one solution to this problem - repatriation,” he said.
Dr Khalilur noted that the position has now gained broad international recognition and that even the Myanmar government has acknowledged the issue, although Bangladesh disagrees with some of the figures provided by Myanmar.
“Not everything in diplomacy is done publicly. Most of it is done behind the scenes. And when there is a success or failure, you see it face to face,” he said.
Assuming the presidency at a time of deepening geopolitical divisions, the Foreign Minister has pledged to make consensus-building and restoring confidence in the UN central to his tenure.
“The UN will commence its ninth decade at a time when trust in our organization is being tested on multiple fronts,” Dr Khalilur told UN member states.
He said the challenges facing the international community were undermining public trust and confidence in the UN’s ability to deliver on its commitments.
“As your president, I will dedicate myself to rebuilding trust, nurturing consensus, and opening space for good-faith negotiations that will lead to outcomes for all that are owned by all,” he said.
Dr Khalilur has also pledged to serve as a bridge-builder among member states, engage all sides, and work to find common ground amid widening divisions.
He said he would uphold the UN Charter and ensure geographical and gender balance within the Office of the President of the General Assembly while remaining attentive to the needs of smaller delegations.
Bangladesh is also expected to use the high-profile presidency to advance issues of national and regional importance, particularly the protracted Rohingya crisis.
State Minister for Foreign Affairs Shama Obaed Islam recently said Dhaka hopes to use its stronger diplomatic position at the UN to intensify international pressure on Myanmar and build momentum for a political and durable solution to the crisis.
“We are trying to involve the international community more,” she said, referring to a high-level UN session on the Rohingya crisis expected to be held in September, with Bangladesh’s Prime Minister Tarique Rahman expected to participate.
Shama Obaed said Dhaka hopes the high-level discussion will produce clearer international guidelines and stronger momentum towards resolving the crisis, which has become increasingly complex amid security and other challenges.
Bangladesh has repeatedly called for sustained international engagement to ensure the safe, voluntary, and dignified return of the Rohingya to Myanmar, while seeking greater global support for addressing the humanitarian and security dimensions of the crisis.

'Friendship' founder Runa Khan wins Ramon Magsaysay Award
item.description:
Runa Khan, founder of Friendship, has been named a recipient of the 2026 Ramon Magsaysay Award for her more than two decades of leadership in developing locally led solutions that empower marginalised communities to live with greater opportunity, dignity and hope.
The Ramon Magsaysay Award is Asia’s premier prize and highest honour—widely regarded as “Asia's Nobel Prize”, recognising “greatness of spirit” and “transformative leadership in Asia”.
Runa Khan is the 14th recipient of the Award from Bangladesh, after, in particular, Muhammad Yunus, founder of Grameen and Mother Teresa from India, both of whom also received the Nobel Prize for Peace. Incidentally, Mother Teresa had travelled to Bangladesh in the nineties and blessed the river barge that would later become Friendship’s first hospital ship. Other outstanding awardees have also been the Fazle Hasan Abed, founder of Brac, the Dalai Lama and Japanese filmmaker Akira Kurasawa. The formal award ceremony will be held on 15 November in Manila, Philippines. On receiving the award, Runa Khan said: “It is with great happiness and profound humility that I accept the Ramon Magsaysay Award. There is no leader who walks alone, so it is an honour for me to receive this on behalf of the unaddressed communities, who allow us to walk beside them; and on behalf of my Friendship family whose tireless devotion makes this work possible every day. I thank also those who have trusted and walked this almost impossible path with me for 25 long years—just believing. My children whose patience and understanding awes me. This recognition is a wonderful responsibility, and I offer my deepest gratitude to the Ramon Magsaysay Award Foundation for their trust and for honouring the enduring faith and power of humanity.” For Runa Khan, the recognition honours a body of work that began in Bangladesh’s remote riverine communities and grew into an integrated model for delivering solutions based on a deep understanding and respect of local communities and their realities. What began with a single floating hospital has grown into a social purpose organisation serving 7.5 million people annually across healthcare, education, climate action, sustainable economic development, inclusive citizenship and cultural preservation. Its holistic approach reflects the interconnected challenges faced by remote communities. Under strong leadership, Friendship’s approach is simple: systems should be designed around people’s realities rather than expecting people to fit systems that cannot reach them. It recruits and trains local people and works with communities to shape the solutions meant for them, taking an inclusive approach by involving women and people with disabilities and connecting health, education, livelihoods, rights and climate resilience. Five years after founding Friendship in Bangladesh, Runa Khan took the initiative to establish Friendship in Luxembourg in 2006, Netherlands in 2007, the UK in 2010, France in 2015, and Belgium in 2018. Her vision was to work as closely as possible with donors and creating partners, thereby bypassing the long chains of intermediaries in international aid while preserving local ownership. That vision has proven to be extremely effective thanks to a strong community of supporters, both public and private. The International entities have stood by the side of Friendship Bangladesh at every stage of its development over the past 24 years.
In her official Ramon Magsaysay Award citation, Runa Khan is being recognised for “her profound empathy for the poorest of the poor in her country, and her courage, vision, and tenacity in building and leading Friendship to accomplish her mission. In her hands, privilege became not an entitlement, but a responsibility; not a family legacy to protect, but a gift to be shared so that others, too, might have the chance to live with hope, opportunity, and dignity.” The Ramon Magsaysay Award was first given in 1958 in memory of the seventh Philippine President Ramon Magsaysay.
In 68 years, the Award has been bestowed on 328 individuals and 28 organisations whose selfless service has offered their societies in 24 countries across Asia, and the rest of the world solutions to some of the most challenging problems of human development.

item.title: Nepal buries dead as rescuers seek thousands missing
item.description:
Nepal was burying on Monday some of the hundreds of bodies retrieved after a deadly, tsunami-like flood crashed through the Himalayan region, sweeping away villages and leaving thousands still missing.
Distraught families have packed rescue stations and hospitals in search of their missing relatives, while others have faced the grim task of identifying bodies at overflowing morgues.
The huge wave of ice, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday claimed at least 797 lives in both Nepal and Tibet -- across the border in China -- with reports of some bodies possibly swept downstream as far as India.
At least 3,048 people remain missing, including many tourists and pilgrims to Tibet's sacred Mount Kailash. There are also 933 workers at hydropower plants among those unaccounted for in Nepal.
Nepali army troops and engineers drilled through debris on Sunday towards workers believed trapped in a tunnel at the Trishuli 3A hydroelectric site in the Himalayan river valley after they successfully inserted a pipe into the passage.
Workers who managed to get out described horrifying scenes when the disaster struck.
Surendra Dowluri, 33, from India's Andhra Pradesh state, said raging water swamped the Upper Trishuli-1 site, where he was working.
"We heard a very loud sound... and saw that the turbine floor was submerged with slush, and six workers were stuck in that," Dowluri told AFP in the Nepali capital Kathmandu after his rescue four days into the disaster.
"We managed to rescue five of them, but one person lost his life," he said, describing how some workers reached higher ground or construction areas out of reach of the torrent.
Overnight rain and rising river waters also hampered rescue operations on Sunday, filling the excavation area with water before conditions eased, the Nepali army said.
The disaster was caused by a glacial collapse, sending a wall of water and debris downstream, the US Geological Survey said.
The torrent caused the formation of huge lakes, closely watched by emergency workers for risks to their operations.
Chinese rescuers near the Tibet border port that was hit by a deadly mudslide were "moved to a safe location" on Sunday after a new lake was formed by a landslide, state media reported.
China has so far put the death toll in Tibet at 16, with the number of missing at 546.
In Nepal, the disaster agency raised the total number of people missing on its side of the border to 2,502 on Sunday, saying there were also 781 confirmed deaths.
Overwhelmed by the number of bodies and without proper freezing facilities, Nepali authorities have had to begin burials before completing the identification process.
Officials said DNA samples were taken from the bodies so that families could later claim them and perform traditional funeral rites.
Grieving relatives gathered at identification centres to watch LED screens showing pictures of retrieved bodies, occasionally closing their eyes when the grim exercise overwhelmed them.
Walking out from one such building next to a makeshift morgue, Shobha Adhikary told a local coordinator she believed one image showed her childhood best friend.
"It looks like him, for sure," she said, showing coordinators a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
"My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta," she said. Geeta has also been missing since Wednesday.
Survivors were also faced with the daunting prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
"All the settlements near the river were swept away," resident Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal's Nuwakot district.
"There is nothing left."
The United States and Canada said they would provide $3.6 million each in humanitarian aid to Nepal.
The UK has offered $6.8 million, while the UN released $2.5 million in emergency funding, and aid pledges were made by the European Union, the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies, and others.
Nepal's economy is already under pressure, with limited resources to respond to a disaster of this scale. Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said the reconstruction bill could run into "billions of dollars".
He appealed for specialised assistance, including heavy-lift drones and technology to help locate people who are trapped.
Khanal also called for forensic testing kits to identify corpses and freezer units to store them, saying bodies that have been in water could decompose at a faster rate.
The minister has highlighted the inequity that Nepal should suffer the extreme impacts of climate change when it has one of the world's lowest per-capita carbon emissions.
That is due to its location in the Himalayas, the world's highest mountain range, where glaciers are melting at rapid speed as the planet heats.
In Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists and where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, a total of 2,141 personnel have joined search and rescue operations.
In an illustration of the difficulties of access, Chinese rescuers seeking to establish a route to the Tibet epicentre of the disaster, Gyirong Port, only advanced 285 metres (935 feet) on Sunday.
They have another 1.25 kilometres to go before reaching the site, the state-run Xinhua news agency reported.

DPDC clarifies prepaid meter charges, ghost bills; urges customers to call 16116
item.description:
The Dhaka Power Distribution Company Limited (DPDC) has urged customers facing abnormal electricity bills, billing discrepancies or unexpected power disconnections to contact its customer service centers or call the hotline 16116 for prompt assistance.
The call comes amid complaints and concerns from customers over deductions of various charges during prepaid meter recharges, unusually high or “ghost” bills, power disconnections at midnight or on holidays, and unusually long tokens generated during the first recharge after a tariff change.
In a notice issued on Monday, DPDC explained different charges and procedures related to prepaid meters and electricity bills to address customers’ concerns and reduce their inconvenience.
It said a demand charge is deducted once a month against the sanctioned load. If a customer does not recharge in a particular month, the demand charges for the months without vending, along with the charge for the current month, are deducted when a customer recharges next.
DPDC said the demand charge also applies to postpaid customers.
Regarding meter rent, the company said no rent is applicable if customers purchase and install their own prepaid meters. If a meter is supplied by DPDC, a monthly rent of Tk 40 applies for a single-phase meter and Tk 250 for a three-phase meter.
A 5% VAT is deducted from the amount recharged each time, in line with the government-set rate applicable to electricity bills.
DPDC said a 200–220-digit token may be generated during the first recharge after a tariff change to activate the new tariff in prepaid meters.
It said this is due to the technical features of the meters and the multiple slabs under different electricity tariff categories.
However, the long token is required only for the first recharge after a tariff change. Subsequent recharges continue to use the usual 20-digit token.
DPDC said it has taken an initiative to bring prepaid meters online to resolve the inconvenience caused by entering long tokens manually.
AMI prepaid meters are currently being installed, which do not require tokens and can be easily recharged through online platforms, including bKash and Rocket.
DPDC said there is no scope for prepaid meters to deduct charges exceeding actual electricity consumption or generate so-called “ghost bills.”
According to the company, the cost of electricity is deducted gradually based on actual consumption and the retail electricity tariff fixed by the Bangladesh Energy Regulatory Commission (BERC).
It said abnormal billing should not occur in prepaid meters unless there is a technical fault, including a common-neutral-related problem.
DPDC said electricity supply is not disconnected even if the prepaid meter balance runs out during weekly holidays or “friendly hours”, defined as 4pm to 10am the following day.
During this period, the meter continues to supply electricity with a negative balance, which is adjusted during the next recharge.
Customers can also activate an emergency balance after their energy balance runs out, allowing them to continue using electricity in emergencies. The amount is subsequently adjusted during the next recharge.
DPDC said customers should not panic if they experience abnormal deductions, billing discrepancies or power disconnections at unexpected times due to technical problems.
Customers are advised to contact the relevant customer service or complaint center, or call DPDC’s hotline at 16116, providing their meter number, customer number and other necessary information.
The company said complaints will be properly verified and, where applicable, necessary corrections and remedial measures will be taken promptly.

item.title: Bangladesh targets 100-plus green-certified ship recycling yards
item.description:
The government has set a target to raise the number of green-certified ship recycling yards in the country to at least three digits (100+), Industries and Commerce Minister Khandakar Abdul Muktadir said on Monday, noting that around 31 such yards currently exist while several more are undergoing green certification.
Muktadir made the remarks as chief guest at a workshop jointly organized by the Ministry of Industries and the International Maritime Organization (IMO) at a hotel in the capital's Karwan Bazar.
The workshop was held to discuss a feasibility study report on setting up a Treatment, Storage and Disposal Facility (TSDF) centre under the "Bangladesh Safe and Environment-Friendly Ship Recycling Project."
Muktadir said Bangladesh remains one of the world's leading countries in ship recycling, having once surpassed even India in tonnage terms. "Although the country has slipped somewhat in recent times, it still holds a significant position in the global ship recycling industry."
Calling the sector vital to the national economy, the minister said it provides employment for a large number of people, while scrap from ships serves as a key raw material source for the country's steel industry.
He stressed that the sector's growth must be ensured in a responsible and environment-friendly manner, adding that the government's goal is to make the industry more modern, safe and sustainable through compliance with international conventions and environmental standards.
To take the number of green-certified yards to a hundred-plus, the minister emphasized technical and financial support alongside effective enforcement of environmental compliance requirements.
Describing hazardous waste management as one of the biggest challenges in ship recycling, Muktadir said large ships generate various hazardous materials and waste during dismantling, which, if not properly managed, pose risks to the environment and public health.
He said the proposed TSDF would play a key role in safely and scientifically collecting, storing, treating and disposing of such waste.
The proposed TSDF is expected to handle a major share of hazardous waste from the ship recycling industry, while also creating scope for managing hazardous waste from other industrial sources, including e-waste.
The minister expressed hope that the facility would help align the sector with international environmental standards and enhance Bangladesh's competitiveness in the global market.
He said a coordinated effort involving the government, yard owners, relevant institutions and international partners could transform the ship recycling sector into a safer, more modern and sustainable industry.

item.title: President stresses stronger BGB role in preventing border killings, smuggling
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on Monday stressed the need for stronger role by Border Guard Bangladesh (BGB) to prevent smuggling, drug trafficking, push-ins and border killings.
He made the call when BGB Director General Major General Mohammad Ashrafuzzaman Siddiqui paid a courtesy call on the president at Bangabhaban.
During the meeting, the BGB DG congratulated President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir on assuming office.
He briefed him on the force’s overall activities and initiatives to enhance surveillance along the borders through the deployment of advanced drones and modern technologies.
President Fakhrul appreciated the BGB’s initiative to introduce advanced technologies to strengthen border security and assured the force of all-out cooperation in this regard.
The president’s secretaries and senior officials were present during the meeting.

item.title: Campaign launched against battery-run autorickshaws in Dhaka-13
item.description:
Authorities have launched a campaign against the illegal operation of battery-run autorickshaws and unauthorised battery-charging establishments in Dhaka-13 following complaints from local residents.
The campaign was launched on Monday on the instructions of State Minister for Primary and Mass Education and Dhaka-13 MP Bobby Hajjaj, according to a press release issued by the ministry.
The press release said residents raised complaints about traffic congestion and the unrestricted movement of battery-run autorickshaws at a town hall meeting in the constituency on Saturday.
Taking the matter seriously, Bobby Hajjaj instructed the relevant authorities to take immediate action.
The campaign began on Sunday, during which authorities took action against a number of battery-run autorickshaws and removed equipment and electrical connections used for unauthorised battery charging.
The initiative aims to restore order on the roads and ensure smoother movement of people in the area, the press release said.
Bobby Hajjaj said the town hall meeting was not merely a platform for hearing complaints but also an effective way to identify citizens’ problems and provide quick solutions.
“We have immediately instructed the relevant authorities to address the issues raised by residents,” he said.
He said necessary measures would continue to ensure normal and smooth movement in Dhaka-13.
The state minister also said coordination between the administration and relevant organisations would be strengthened to address residents’ concerns.
“Work is underway to make Dhaka-13 a more liveable and people-friendly area by giving importance to citizens’ complaints and suggestions,” he said.
Local residents expressed satisfaction with the swift action following their complaints at the town hall meeting, according to the press release.

item.title: Nepal-Tibet floods: Death toll crosses 900, nearly 5,000 missing
item.description:
Rescuers struggled Monday through mud and debris for a sixth day, as the number of missing people soared to nearly 5,000 since tsunami-like glacial floods roared down from the China-Nepal border, creating an “unimaginable” disaster.
The latest confirmed death toll surged above 900, but the number of those unaccounted for is also climbing -- with unidentified bodies buried in mass graves after DNA sampling.
The huge wave of freezing water, rocks and debris that smashed into villages and towns on Wednesday killed at least 903 people in Nepal and in Tibet, in China, with at least 17 bodies pulled from rivers downstream in India.
Late Sunday Nepali Prime Minster Balendra Shah called the disaster “unimaginable and heartbreaking.”
Rescue teams are in a race against time in treacherous conditions in a bid to free dozens of hydropower workers believed trapped in tunnels -- digging, drilling and blasting through debris, a non-stop effort supported by teams from China, India and South Korea.
So far, three dead bodies have been pulled out of two tunnels, and the teams have found routes blocked with mud.
Amid the horror, there has been some hope; a six-year-old pulled out of the mud four days after the disaster on Friday was reunited with her parents after police found her crying for her mother.
“Her body was trapped in mud, but her head was outside,” Nepali Armed Police spokesman Netra Bahadur Karki told AFP.
“She is out of danger and recovering at a hospital and has reunited with her family.”
The disaster was sparked by a glacial collapse, the US Geological Survey said. While the exact cause of that collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, raising the risk of such disasters.
Nepali Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal said: “The people of Nepal are one of the major victims of the changing climate and its impact.”
Scientists say the Himalayas, the world’s highest mountain range, are melting faster as global temperatures rise.
Aid needs are enormous. Entire communities have been swept away, leaving families homeless in heavy rain or sheltering in temporary facilities.
“This is an unfolding disaster,” UN children’s fund official Abiodun Banire told AFP, saying the needs of the tens of thousands impacted were vast.
Roads have been washed away, power plants destroyed and dozens of bridges smashed.
“We are continuing to work for search, rescue and relief operations,” Karki told AFP on Monday, as communications slowly improved. Police initially had to use drones to carry messages into cut-off areas.
“Rescue teams have now reached most areas, by road or by helicopters,” he added.
With mortuaries overflowing with the dead, Nepal has begun burying some of the hundreds of bodies recovered after taking DNA samples so families can later retrieve them.
Kathmandu has appealed for international support, saying Nepal needed “more than a thousand” freezer units to store bodies.
Distraught families, desperate for news of missing relatives, are watching images of bodies on screens at community centers in a bid to identify the dead.
Shobha Adhikary, in the southern Nepali city of Bharatpur, told a local coordinator she believed one image showed her childhood best friend.
“It looks like him, for sure,” she said, showing a photograph of a smiling, middle-aged man.
“My husband and I are best friends with Rajkumar and his wife Geeta,” she said. Geeta has also been missing since Wednesday.
Among Nepal’s list of the missing are 592 foreigners, including tourists who had come for trekking in its apparently serene mountains, and Hindu pilgrims seeking spiritual peace at Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
Nepali army rescuers said Monday its teams were working to “clear water, mud and sediment” as they dug to reach around 100 workers that the government believes may be alive inside multiple tunnels.
They are among the 933 workers at hydropower plants unaccounted for in Nepal. Workers who managed to get out described horrifying scenes when the disaster struck.

item.title: China’s Xi and Iran’s Pezeshkian in Kyrgyzstan, Putin expected
item.description:
China’s Xi Jinping and Iranian President Massoud Pezeshkian were in Kyrgyzstan for a summit of the Shanghai Cooperation Organization, with Russia’s Vladimir Putin expected later on Monday for the two-day event that will involve over a dozen other leaders.
The regional SCO bloc -- which seeks to be a counterinfluence to the West -- is celebrating its 25-year anniversary.
The group brings together Russia, China, India, Pakistan, Iran, four Central Asian countries and Moscow-allied Belarus.
Arriving in Bishkek on Sunday, Xi hailed what he described as a “golden period” in relations with Central Asian Kyrgyzstan, as China deepens its influence in the historically Russia-dominated region.
Putin and Xi have previously used SCO summits to promote their vision of a multipolar world and present a united front against the West.
It takes place four-and-a-half years into Moscow’s Ukraine invasion and six months into the war between Washington and Tehran.
Iran’s Pezeshkian also arrived in Bishkek, Tehran’s media reported.
Putin, Xi and Pezeshkian, as well as India’s Narendra Modi and Pakistan’s Shehbaz Sharif, are due to take part in a plenary session chaired by Kyrgyz leader Sadyr Japarov.
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan is also expected to attend, although his country is not a formal member.
Putin is also due to hold separate bilateral talks with Pezeshkian and Xi, among other leaders, Kremlin spokesman Yuri Ushakov said.
Russia and Iran -- among the most sanctioned states in the world -- have massively deepened their military and economic ties since Moscow invaded Ukraine.
US President Donald Trump has warned Moscow and Beijing against arming Iran.
Putin’s meeting with Pezeshkian comes days after the CIA’s director John Ratcliffe made a rare trip to Moscow, with US media speculating he could have discussed Ukraine and Iran with his Russian counterparts.
The SCO has historically focused on economic issues but has gained momentum in recent years under Moscow’s and Beijing’s leadership.
On top of its 10 members, it now has 15 “dialogue partners,” including Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Qatar.
It also has two observer countries -- Afghanistan and Mongolia.
The SCO’s founding declaration says the group is “not an alliance directed against other states.”
But Putin and Xi have repeatedly made anti-Western speeches during its summits.
At last year’s gathering, Putin accused Western countries of provoking the Ukraine war, while Xi denounced “acts of intimidation,” referring to US-Chinese tensions.
The Bishkek summit takes place at a time when some SCO members are in the midst of real wars -- the Ukraine and Iran conflicts -- or trade wars, with the imposition of US tariffs on Chinese and Indian goods.
This month, the US slapped secondary sanctions on Iran’s trading partners in the sectors of gold, technology, digital assets, aviation and maritime transport, aiming to cripple Tehran’s economy.
Washington has also threatened Iran’s allies with sanctions.
China, a major importer of Iranian oil, responded by saying it would “firmly defend” its interests.
Iran, living under sanctions since its 1979 revolution ended with Islamic authorities taking charge, has regularly said it will not cave to economic pressure.
But Pezeshkian has acknowledged his country faces “economic difficulties.”
Iran only joined the bloc in 2023.
Mohammad Hassan Najmi, an international relations expert, told AFP that Tehran “believes its membership and active participation in these alliances can enable it to circumvent US and European sanctions.”
But concrete benefits of the group are uncertain, he said, as “in times of crisis, these alliances have rarely allowed Iran to resolve its difficulties.”
While the bloc claims to represent some 40 percent of the world’s population and 25 percent of global GDP, it remains diverse, with some disagreements among members.
Russia and China compete for influence in Central Asia -- a resource-rich region crucial for the transport of goods between Europe and Asia -- while Beijing has at times had strained relations with India and Pakistan.

England v Pakistan second Test: Three talking points
item.description:
England thrashed Pakistan by 194 runs to win the second Test at Lord's on Sunday and so take an unbeatable 2-0 lead in a three-match campaign.
Below AFP Sport looks at three talking points that emerged as England completed their first multi-match Test series win in over a year.
Relentless Robinson
The present England management have sometimes given the impression the only thing that matters in a pace attack is sheer speed.
But Ollie Robinson has demonstrated the importance of accuracy and movement as well.
Robinson lacks the express pace and physical threat of Sussex and England team-mate Jofra Archer.
But the seamer's range of skills were on display at Lord's where, albeit helped by a green-tinged pitch, Robinson was named player-of-the-match for a haul of 8-35 that included a remarkable 4-11 in 13 overs during Pakistan's first innings.
While concerns over his fitness and questions regarding some social media posts have threatened to derail his England career, there have rarely been any doubts over the 32-year-old Robinson's talent.
In his three Tests this season the Sussex captain has taken 23 wickets at a stunningly low average of 8.34, with England skipper Joe Root saying on Sunday Robinson was "horrendous (to face) in these conditions."
Pitch problems a worry for Lord's
The way England opener Emilio Gay fell lbw for 31 to a 'pea-shooter' delivery from Pakistan paceman Mohammad Abbas was the kind of dismissal that really should not happen on the third day of a Test and certainly not at a ground that styles itself as the Home of Cricket.
For Gay, struggling to cement his place in the England side, it was a particularly cruel exit as what should be a game of skill was turned into a lottery by uneven bounce.
It was also a worrying sign for Marylebone Cricket Club, the owners of Lord's.
The pitch for the previous Test at Lord's, against New Zealand, was rated as "unsatisfactory" by the International Cricket Council, with next year's World Test Championship final relocated across London to the Oval partly as a consequence.
And while previous surfaces at Lord's, renowned for its steep slope across the ground, faced criticism for being bland and too much in favour of the batsmen, clearly there are limits.
MCC recognised they had an issue after the New Zealand match, announcing the creation of "an agronomy advisory group" and a "phased pitch-relaying programme", although any benefits from may not be seen for several years and are unlikely to be of much consolation to Gay.
Shakeel salvages some batting respect for Pakistan
Pakistan have yet to make 200 so far this series, with the tourists dismissed for 171 and 135 during an innings and 103-run defeat in the first Test at Headingley before managing 110 and 194 at Lord's.
But that Pakistan, already bottom of the World Test Championship table before this latest thumping loss, at least got close to a benchmark total on Sunday was largely down to Saud Shakeel's enterprising 97.
Coming in with Pakistan in dire straits at 14-3, he initially scored briskly without taking undue risks before a flurry of thrilling boundaries, including two superb hooked sixes off fast bowler Josh Tongue took him to within sight of a hundred.
Shakeel fell just short of what would have been his fifth century in 25 Tests when he holed out off Tongue, the left-hander failing to join Abbas on the Lord's honours boards following the veteran seamer's five-wicket haul earlier Sunday.
"In the batting, we weren't up to the mark (in the first innings)," said Babar Azam, the Pakistan captain. "Saud Shakeel showed his class and dedication in the second innings."

Dhaka's air unhealthy for sensitive groups
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 11th among the world's most polluted cities on Monday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 102 at 9:30am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as 'Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups,' posing minor health risks to vulnerable people.
Malaysia's Kuching topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 370.
Kuwait's Kuwait City and India's Delhi occupied the second and third spots, with AQI scores of 227 and 221, respectively.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered ‘unhealthy for sensitive groups’, 151 to 200 ‘unhealthy’, 201 to 300 ‘very unhealthy’, while levels above 301 are deemed ‘hazardous’, posing serious health risks.
The AQI, which provides daily updates on air quality, indicates how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically worsening in winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly due to stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: Early winter vegetables bring hope for Rajshahi farmers
item.description:
Farmers in Rajshahi’s Paba upazila are busy cultivating early varieties of winter vegetables, hoping to bring their produce to market before the regular winter season and secure higher prices.
Among them is Mosharraf Hossain of Ashgram village, who has cultivated cauliflower and cabbage on 32 bighas of land this season. He has already sold vegetables from 7.5 bighas and made a profit of around Tk1.5 lakh per bigha.
During a visit to his fields in Ashgram under Damkura union on Saturday morning, Mosharraf was seen tending to his cauliflower and cabbage plants. He was putting soil around the plants, applying fertiliser and removing weeds.
Mosharraf said he cultivated the early varieties with advice and support from the Paba upazila agriculture office.
He planted around 6,000 cauliflower and cabbage plants per bigha, while his production costs were around Tk40,000–45,000 per bigha.
“There are risks in cultivating early vegetables. Around 2,000 plants per bigha can be damaged. But if we can bring the vegetables to market at the right time, we get good prices,” he said.
“Last year, I made a good profit from early vegetables. That is why I have expanded cultivation this year,” he added.
Mosharraf said he has already sold cauliflower from three bighas and cabbage from another 4.5 bighas.
The vegetables have generally sold for Tk50–70 per piece, while he received as much as Tk90 at times. After deducting production, cultivation and marketing costs, he made around Tk1.5 lakh in profit per bigha.
He has another 25 bighas under cauliflower and cabbage cultivation, which he expects to harvest within a few weeks.
Farmers say early winter vegetables can fetch better prices because their supply remains limited before the regular winter season begins.
Normally, supplies of cauliflower, cabbage, radish, carrot and other winter vegetables increase between November and January, putting downward pressure on prices.
Farmer Nazrul Islam of Alimganj has cultivated 4,000 heads of early cabbage on 12 kathas of land this season at a cost of around Tk18,000–20,000.
He has already sold 200 heads at Tk30 each. If prices remain favourable, he expects to earn around Tk1 lakh from the remaining crop, leaving him with a profit of nearly Tk80,000 after expenses.
Nazrul also cultivated tomatoes last year, earning around Tk5 lakh from five bighas of land.
This year, following advice from the agriculture department, he has cultivated an early variety of tomato on 10 kathas. The plants have already started flowering, and he expects to bring the crop to market around the middle of Ashwin.
Early vegetable cultivation is also gaining momentum in Haripur, Harian, Damkura, Parila, Bargachhi, Naohata and Paikpara areas of Paba.
Farmers are cultivating cauliflower, cabbage, beans, radish, carrot, eggplant, bitter gourd, teasel gourd, bottle gourd, red amaranth and coriander, among other vegetables.
Mizanur Rahman, a farmer from Paikpara village under Naohata municipality, has cultivated early varieties of cauliflower and cabbage on 1.5 bighas.
“I expect to bring the vegetables to market within the next 20 to 25 days,” he said.
Paba Upazila Agriculture Officer MA Mannan said the target for vegetable cultivation in the upazila this season was 1,895 hectares and that the target had already been achieved.
“A significant portion of the cultivation consists of early varieties. Farmers are selecting crops by considering market demand, production costs and possible selling prices,” he said.
“Earlier, agriculture was for survival. Now agriculture is becoming a business,” Mannan said.
He added that farmers were being encouraged to cultivate early vegetables and use bio-pesticides. They were also being advised to follow approved doses when using chemical pesticides.
Meanwhile, the Department of Agricultural Extension (DAE) has set a target of cultivating vegetables on 6,430 hectares of land across Rajshahi district this season.
DAE Rajshahi Deputy Director Mustafa Kamal Hossain said cultivation of early varieties had increased by 200 hectares compared with previous years.
With the regular winter vegetable season still weeks away, farmers in Paba are now racing against time to get their produce to market early and take advantage of potentially higher prices.

The Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) has summoned former army chief General (retd) SM Shafiuddin Ahmed for questioning over allegations of acquiring illegal assets through various irregularities and corruption.
He has been asked to appear at the ACC headquarters at 12:30pm on September 14 to provide his statement.
ACC Public Relations Officer Aktarul Islam confirmed the matter to Dhaka Tribune on Sunday.
According to a notice signed by ACC Director Md Abul Hasnat, the commission is investigating allegations of Shafiuddin Ahmed acquiring illegal assets through “various irregularities and corruption.”
The ACC has formed a two-member investigation team to look into the allegations, with Director Abul Hasnat as team leader and Deputy Director Mozammil Hossain as a member.
The notice said it was necessary to hear and record Shafiuddin Ahmed’s statement for the proper investigation of the allegations. He has therefore been asked to appear at the ACC headquarters on the scheduled date with a photocopy of his national identity card.
According to ACC records, the investigation into the allegations against Shafiuddin Ahmed began on December 14, 2025.
General (retd) SM Shafiuddin Ahmed took charge as chief of the Bangladesh Army on June 24, 2021, succeeding General (retd) Aziz Ahmed. He retired on June 23, 2024, after serving as army chief for three years.
During his tenure as army chief, he also served as president of the Bangladesh Olympic Association.

item.title: Killed over Tk20: Man gets life term 25 years later
item.description:
A Dhaka court has sentenced a man to life imprisonment for stabbing Biplob alias Bashir to death over Tk20 in Gopibagh, Demra, now under Wari police station, 25 years ago.
Judge Zahidul Islam of Dhaka Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge Court-13 delivered the verdict on Sunday.
The court also fined Monir Hossain Tk20,000, with three months of rigorous imprisonment in default, said court bench assistant Sohel Mia.
As Monir has been absconding, the court issued an arrest warrant against him as well as a warrant for execution of the sentence, Sohel said.
According to the case documents, on December 4, 2001. Monir stabbed Biplob alias Bashir, 18, in different parts of his body.
Hearing Biplob scream, one Nazir Ahmed, who was at a nearby mosque, and several others caught Monir. Biplob was taken to Monowara Hospital and later shifted to National Hospital, where the attending physician declared him dead.
Nazir Ahmed filed a murder case with Demra police station the same day. Monir was subsequently arrested and sent to jail.
After investigating the case, Demra police station Sub-Inspector A Jabbar submitted a charge sheet against Monir on March 31, 2002.
The investigation found that Biplob had borrowed Tk20 from Monir and that Monir killed him after Biplob failed to repay the money.
The court framed charges against Monir on September 3, 2002, and began the trial. During the proceedings, the court recorded the statements of five witnesses.
Monir was granted bail in 2009. However, after he remained absent, the court cancelled his bail and issued an arrest warrant on October 31, 2013.
As Monir remained absconding, he could not participate in the hearing of his defence.

item.title: Moyeen Khan: Govt giving highest priority to dengue prevention
item.description:
Local Government, Rural Development (LGRD) and Cooperatives Minister Dr Abdul Moyeen Khan on Sunday said the government is giving the highest priority to preventing the spread of dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases.
“Efforts are being made to destroy mosquito breeding grounds, while research and technical capabilities are being strengthened to enhance the effectiveness of mosquito-control medicines,” he said while addressing an emergency meeting of the National Taskforce Committee formed to prevent dengue and other mosquito-borne diseases at the meeting room of the Local Government Division at the Secretariat.
State Minister for LGRD and Cooperatives Mir Shahe Alam presided over the meeting.
Moyeen Khan said there are various challenges in controlling mosquitoes in large and densely populated areas such as Dhaka North and South City Corporations and Gazipur. Despite limited resources, the city corporations are making all-out efforts, he added.
He said places where mosquitoes breed must be identified and measures taken to prevent water from accumulating there.
The minister further said that research and reviews on the effectiveness of mosquito-control medicines are being conducted in cooperation with Japan and other developed countries. Relevant experts from universities have also been involved in the work, he added.
He stressed the need to strengthen technical capabilities alongside raising public awareness to contain the spread of dengue.
At the meeting, State Minister Mir Shahe Alam said the number of dengue patients has fallen by nearly half this year compared with last year.
He said cleanliness drives, spraying and awareness-raising activities are being conducted in various city corporations to control mosquitoes.
According to information provided by the state minister, around 90 people have died while undergoing treatment after contracting dengue from January this year until yesterday.
Alam urged people to regularly clean discarded tyres, plastic containers and other places where water can accumulate in their homes, on rooftops and balconies, and in surrounding areas.
He said public awareness, alongside government initiatives, will play an important role in preventing dengue.
Secretaries of the Local Government Division and the Health Division, the administrator of Dhaka South City Corporation, officials concerned from Dhaka North and South City Corporations, chief health officers of 13 city corporations and other relevant officials attended the meeting.
Officials from 11 city corporations outside Dhaka joined the meeting virtually.

item.title: Dhaka, Beijing set to launch strategic defence dialogues
item.description:
Bangladesh and China on Sunday discussed cooperation on the Teesta River Comprehensive Management and Restoration, the early launching of a Foreign Minister-level Strategic Dialogue, and the beginning of State Minister-level Diplomacy and Defense Dialogue.
The two countries discussed a wide range of issues of mutual interest, including initiating the process for the export of jackfruit and guava from Bangladesh to China, the China-Bangladesh-Myanmar Economic Corridor, and cooperation on the Rohingya issue.
The issues came up during a courtesy meeting between Chinese Ambassador to Bangladesh Yao Wen and State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on Sunday.
During the meeting, State Minister Kobir described China as a trusted friend and valued strategic partner of Bangladesh and reaffirmed Bangladesh’s commitment to the "One China Policy."
He expressed satisfaction with the renewed momentum in bilateral relations and the elevation of Bangladesh-China ties to a “China-Bangladesh Community with a Shared Future” following Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s recent successful visit to China.
Ambassador Yao Wen congratulated State Minister Kobir on his assumption of office and sought his support to advance further the longstanding and close relationship between Bangladesh and China.
He also conveyed felicitations from China’s Executive Deputy Foreign Minister to State Minister Kobir.
Ambassador Wen briefed the state minister on developments concerning the outcomes of the prime minister’s recent visit to China, including the groundbreaking of the China Economic and Industrial Zone (CEIZ), the signing of a commercial contract for the modernization of Mongla Port, and possible cooperation on the establishment of a Mongla Export Processing Zone (EPZ).
He noted that the CEIZ is expected to attract around 30 Chinese companies with an investment of approximately US$500 million, creating an estimated 100,000 job opportunities for local Bangladeshis.
Ambassador Wen further briefed State Minister Kobir on upcoming high-level exchanges and visits, including the planned visits to Bangladesh by the Vice President of the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA), the Minister of the International Department of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China (IDCPC), and the Executive Vice Governor of Yunnan Province.
The Chinese ambassador also extended an invitation to State Minister-1 Kobir to visit China in October this year.
