item.title: President: Enforced disappearance perpetrators must face justice
item.description:
President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has said all criminals involved in enforced disappearances should be brought to justice, no matter how powerful they are.
“There would be no more ‘Aynaghar’ in independent Bangladesh and every criminal involved in enforced disappearance must receive the maximum punishment under the law,” he said.
The president said this while addressing an event on Sunday marking the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances-2026 as the chief guest.
Organized by the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs, the discussion was held at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Centre in Dhaka.
The president said during the past one and a half decades under the fascist government, the unbearable grip of enforced disappearance and secret detention centre ‘Aynaghar’ had weighed heavily on Bangladesh.
“Those who protested against injustice, expressed dissent, or remained vocal on the streets to demand democratic rights were picked up to silence them and were subjected to enforced disappearance and killings. Yet, the state institutions subservient to the fascists continued to deny those heinous crimes,” he added.
Mirza Fakhrul said that in the backdrop of the mass uprising of unarmed students and people, the fascist ruler was forced to flee the country. Now, reparation measures must be taken instead of revenge, and the real criminals must be brought under the law.
The president noted that all avenues of returning fascism to this country would be permanently closed. He said enforced disappearance is not merely taking away a person. It takes away the smiles, peace, dreams, and economic and social well-being of their beloved ones.
“It is a heinous violation of human rights. The constitution of the country has guaranteed rights of every citizen to live, enjoy liberty anf getting protection of law. Through enforced disappearances and killings, all these rights are violated at once,” he noted.
“I believe the state’s responsibility will not end merely by punishing the criminals,” he said, urging the government to stand beside the victims and families of enforced disappearance by ensuring their dignity, social security, healthcare, education, livelihood, and rehabilitation.
The president said the establishment of a culture of enforced disappearance and killing is a deeply painful and humiliating chapter in our national history.
He mentioned the incidents of enforced disappearance during the fascist regime, including Ilias Ali, Chowdhury Alam, Sajedul Islam, incumbent home minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Barrister Arman and retired Lieutenant General Azmi saying countless dissidents, officials, writers, journalists, social workers, and even housewives and ordinary citizens were subjected to disappearance.
The president said former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia had always been vocal against enforced disappearances and killings by the fascist government.
Many leaders of BNP, Jamaat-e-Islami, social entities, media, civil society members, and people from all walks of life fell victim of enforced disappearance and killings during the fascist regime, he said.
The president also remembered Sanjida Islam Tulee, convener of Mayer Dak, who had been vocal against enforced disappearances during the fascist era.
“We want a Bangladesh where there will be political differences, but no political vengeance. There will be freedom of expression, but no culture of fear. There will be law and order, but no injustice in the name of law. The state will have power, but that power will remain under the control of the Constitution and the law,” he said.
"Alongside economic growth, the true picture of a state’s development and success is reflected in how it practices democracy, how much it’s based on justice and humanity, and how safe its citizens' lives are," he said.
Liberation War Affairs Minister Ahmed Aazam Khan presided over the event while Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, Law Minister Md. Asaduzzaman and State Minister for the Ministry of Liberation War Affairs Ishraque Hossain were present as special guests. Victims of enforced disappearances also lawmakers Humam Quader Chowdhury, Anisur Rahaman, Tahsina Rushdir, Sanjida Islam, Mir Ahmad Binquasem spoke on the occasion and demanded a fair trial of the incidents of enforced disappearances.

item.title: Ex-IGP Enamul Huq passes away
item.description:
Former Inspector General of Police (IGP) M Enamul Huq passed away at a hospital in the capital on Sunday. He was 88.
He breathed his last in the early hours, according to a press release issued by Police Headquarters.
Enamul is survived by his wife, two sons and a daughter.
A namaz-e-janaza for him was held after Zohr prayers at the SI Shiru Miah Auditorium in the Rajarbagh Police Lines, followed by an official state funeral.
He will be laid to rest at his family graveyard in Godagari upazila of Rajshahi district.
Additional Inspector General (AIG) AKM Awlad Hossain laid a wreath at the coffin on behalf of IGP Md Ali Hossain Fakir. Tributes were also paid on behalf of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), Bangladesh Police Service Association and the Retired Police Officers' Welfare Association.
Enamul served as IGP from October 16, 1991 to July 8, 1992.
During his distinguished career, he also served as the DMP commissioner, the principal of the Bangladesh Police Academy in Sarda, Rajshahi and a member of the Law Commission of Bangladesh.
Enamul was the only elected member of Interpol from Bangladesh from 1988 to 1992. He also worked with various United Nations agencies.
He was also an accomplished writer who authored approximately 14 books and regularly wrote columns for national and international publications.
Meanwhile, IGP Ali Hossain and the Bangladesh Police Service Association expressed deep shock at the death of the former IGP.

item.title: Appellate Division: Writ not maintainable where contract provides for arbitration
item.description:
The Appellate Division of the Supreme Court has held that where a contract provides for arbitration, mediation or another alternative mechanism to resolve disputes arising after its execution, a party cannot bypass that mechanism and directly file a writ petition with the High Court.
The observation came in a judgment published on the Supreme Court website on Sunday.
The Appellate Division made the observation while dismissing a civil appeal challenging an earlier judgment concerning the execution of a contract through negotiation or settlement.
The court said that where a contract provides an effective alternative remedy for resolving a dispute, there is no scope for directly invoking the High Court's writ jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution.
The judgment was delivered in the case of M/s AMS Faraz Construction vs State.
The full 37-page judgment, delivered on February 22 by a five-member bench headed by Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury, was published on August 25.
The judgment said that even when a statutory authority is a party to a contract involving the sale of government assets, a party that has violated the terms of the contract cannot seek redress by filing a writ petition. Where the contract contains an effective arbitration clause or provides another alternative mechanism for dispute resolution, the party must pursue that remedy before seeking relief under Article 102.
According to the case documents, Chisty Textile Mills was established in 1966 on about 16 acres of land in Daulatpur of Adarsha Sadar upazila in Comilla. The mill was nationalized in 1972.
Production at the factory was later suspended and its workers were dismissed under a golden handshake scheme. Bangladesh Textile Mills Corporation (BTMC) subsequently resumed operations, but the mill was eventually closed amid continued losses. On November 9, 2003, the government decided to liquidate it.
After a liquidator was appointed to sell the state-owned mill, Md Faruk Islam Bhuiyan, proprietor of AMS Faraz Construction Ltd of Ganganagar in Kasba upazila, Brahmanbaria, expressed interest in purchasing it.
The Ministry of Textiles and Jute subsequently valued the mill at Tk35 crore and signed an agreement with Faraz Construction on January 1, 2014. Under the agreement, the company was required to pay Tk15 crore as a down payment and the remaining Tk20 crore in five equal instalments.
The government handed over the mill and its land to Faraz Construction on January 9, 2014.
However, allegations later surfaced that the factory had been sold without a tender or open auction and at a price significantly below its actual value.
Several national dailies reported on February 11, 2014, alleging irregularities in the liquidation process and claiming that property worth Tk350 crore had been sold for Tk35 crore.
The government subsequently issued an order directing Faruk Islam Bhuiyan to refrain from carrying out activities related to the mill and stopped accepting the outstanding instalments. Faraz Construction had already defaulted on the second instalment.
Faraz Construction later sought withdrawal of the order, but the government rejected its request. Following instructions from the Prime Minister's Office, BTMC issued an order on April 17, 2014, suspending all activities at the mill until further instructions.
Faraz Construction subsequently sought withdrawal of the suspension order. After receiving a response, the company served a legal notice and later filed a writ petition with the High Court in 2014 after receiving no further response.
The High Court issued a rule and, after hearing both sides, disposed of it on June 15, 2015, with several directions.
The High Court directed the authorities to allow Faraz Construction to resume operations at Chisty Textile Mills and to accept the remaining instalments. It also directed the execution and registration of the necessary sale deed in favour of Faraz Construction in accordance with the law and the terms of the January 1, 2014 agreement with BTMC.
The government subsequently appealed against the High Court judgment. On July 3, 2018, the Appellate Division set aside the High Court judgment and order.
Faraz Construction filed a civil review petition against the Appellate Division judgment in 2019. The petition was accepted for hearing on March 6, 2025. On February 22, 2026, the five-member Appellate Division bench dismissed the review petition.
In its judgment, the Appellate Division said the liquidator had no authority under the agreement to sell the mill through any process other than a tender or open auction.
Therefore, once the agreement was executed, the mill could not be transferred without following the procedure prescribed in the agreement. The court also observed that the process followed for transferring the mill did not comply with the law.
The court said the appellants themselves had violated important terms and conditions of the agreement and therefore could not seek legal remedy through a writ petition based on the alleged agreement.
The judgment further said that when parties to a contract choose arbitration as the forum for resolving disputes arising from the agreement, a party cannot bypass that mechanism and seek direct enforcement of the contract under Article 102 of the Constitution.
“In this context, this division is of the opinion that where a dispute arises out of an obligation to comply with a contract and the contract itself provides for settlement of the dispute through arbitration or any other forum, the aggrieved party should pursue the remedy prescribed in the contract without invoking the exceptional jurisdiction of the High Court Division under Article 102 of the Constitution,” the judgment said.
The court also noted that Faraz Construction had failed to comply with the payment schedule under the contract and had not pursued the arbitration mechanism provided in the agreement.
Finding no manifest error in the judgment under review, the Appellate Division dismissed the civil appeal.

item.title: Rangpur murders: Siddharth’s father, brother released
item.description:
Police have released Siddharth Das’s father, Binoy Das, and elder brother, Partha Das, after questioning them in connection with the murder of former Rangpur Zilla School teacher Ganapati Chakraborty and three members of his family in the Masuapara area of Rangpur city.
Police detained the two from their homes on Saturday night and took them to the Metropolitan Detective Branch (DB) office, where they were questioned for about four hours.
Deputy Commissioner of Police of Rangpur Metropolitan DB Sanatan Chakraborty confirmed the matter.
According to DB police, shortly after the bodies of Ganapati and his family members were recovered on August 22, two suspects, Mugdha Das and Siddharth Das, were detained. They later gave confessional statements under Section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, admitting their direct involvement in the four murders.
Police subsequently asked Siddharth’s father and brother to appear at the DB office for questioning, but they did not do so. They were later detained from their homes on Saturday night.
Sanatan Chakraborty said important information was obtained from the two during questioning and would be verified and reviewed.
“For now, they have been released on bond. If necessary, they will be questioned again,” he said.
After their release, Binoy Das and Partha Das told reporters that they had not been mistreated by police. They said they were questioned about the incident and provided all the information they knew.

Born on May 31, 1962, Justice Md Habibul Gani obtained MSS and LLB degrees from the University of Chittagong.

item.title: Dhaka records moderate air quality Sunday morning
item.description:
Dhaka ranked 42th among the world's most polluted cities on Sunday morning, recording an Air Quality Index (AQI) score of 58 at 9:15am.
According to the AQI scale, the city's air quality was classified as "moderate", posing moderate health concerns for a very small number of unusually sensitive individuals (such as people with asthma, heart disease, or older adults).
Kuching of Malaysia topped the global pollution list with an AQI score of 297, followed by Delhi in India with 180 and Doha in Qatar with 167.
According to AQI standards, a reading between 101 and 150 is considered "unhealthy for sensitive groups", 151 to 200 "unhealthy", 201 to 300 "very unhealthy", while levels above 301 are deemed "hazardous", posing serious health risks.
The AQI, which provides daily updates on air quality, indicates how clean or polluted the air is and highlights potential health impacts.
In Bangladesh, the AQI is calculated based on five major pollutants: particulate matter (PM10 and PM2.5), nitrogen dioxide (NO2), carbon monoxide (CO), sulfur dioxide (SO2), and ozone.
Dhaka has long struggled with air pollution, with air quality typically worsening in winter and improving during the monsoon season.
The World Health Organization estimates that air pollution causes around seven million deaths globally each year, mainly due to stroke, heart disease, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, lung cancer and acute respiratory infections.

item.title: ASK demands accountability over new disappearance allegations
item.description:
Ain o Salish Kendra (ASK) has called for independent, impartial and effective investigations into all allegations of enforced disappearance, saying state accountability is essential to prevent such incidents from recurring.
The human rights organization made the call amid new allegations of enforced disappearance in Bangladesh in 2026, despite the country's accession to the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance (ICPPED) in 2024.
The family of a man, Miraj Sheikh, has alleged that he remains missing after being taken away by members of the Coast Guard in Mongla, Bagerhat.
ASK said the allegation must be promptly and impartially investigated to establish the truth about his fate and whereabouts.
The organization said enacting laws alone would not be enough to end enforced disappearances. Missing persons must be traced, while victims and their families must be ensured the right to know the truth.
ASK also called for establishing the truth about past incidents and ensuring accountability, while developing effective state protection mechanisms to prevent enforced disappearances from recurring in the future.
The information was provided in a press release sent by ASK on Saturday.
To prevent and provide remedies for enforced disappearances, the government has approved the draft Prevention and Remedies for Enforced Disappearance Act, 2026, in the cabinet.
ASK welcomed the initiative but said concerns raised by human rights activists and relevant stakeholders regarding some provisions of the draft should be given serious consideration.
It said the law would be more effective and acceptable if the opinions of victims and their families, human rights organizations, lawyers and relevant experts were considered before the law is finalized.
On August 30, 2024, Bangladesh acceded to the ICPPED. ASK said the move represented an important international commitment by the state to prevent enforced disappearances and provide remedies for victims.
However, ASK said that despite Bangladesh joining the convention, new allegations of enforced disappearance have emerged in the country in 2026.
Expressing solidarity with all victims of enforced disappearance and their families, ASK called for an end to enforced disappearances, the establishment of the truth about the fate and whereabouts of missing persons, and the protection of every citizen under the law.
Sunday is the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances. The day is observed to express solidarity with victims and their families, call for an end to such serious human rights violations, and reiterate the demand to establish the truth about the fate and whereabouts of missing persons.
ASK said this year's observance carries special significance as 20 years have passed since the United Nations adopted the ICPPED in 2006.
This year's theme, “Victims first. Actions now,” calls for immediate and effective action by prioritizing the rights and dignity of victims.
Bangladesh has also experienced allegations of enforced disappearances and their severe humanitarian consequences over a long period.

item.title: Draft law on enforced disappearances awaits National Parliament passage
item.description:
The draft of the proposed “Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act, 2026," is now available on the website of the Ministry of Home Affairs for public opinion.
After getting public opinion the draft will be given final approval by the National Parliament.
This landmark legislation seeks to fulfill the state's commitment to human rights, individual liberty, and the rule of law which proposed enforced disappearance as a criminal offense and comprehensive punishment.
The draft defines the arrest, detention, or abduction of any individual by a government official or a member of the disciplined forces such as army, navy, air force, police, RAB, BGB, and intelligence agencies followed by a refusal to acknowledge the act or concealment of the victim’s fate as enforced disappearance.
The law explicitly states that enforced disappearance is a ‘continuous offense’, meaning it remains active until the victim's location, condition, or fate is officially confirmed.
Furthermore, no situation, including state security, political instability, or a state of emergency, can be used as a justification for such crime.
Conviction for enforced disappearance carries a maximum life term imprisonment and a fine up to Tk50 lakh.
In case of death of a disappeared person, or if the body is found or remain missing for more than five years, the responsible persons have to face the death penalty or life imprisonment, along with a fine up to Taka one crore.
The draft also proposed a minimum five years in prison for keeping a person confined in a secret detention center or intentional destruction or tampering the evidence related to the disappearance.
A major feature of the law is the introduction of command responsibility. Superiors or commanders of the disciplined forces will be held criminally liable if the disappearance is occurred in their consciousness or they ignored information about this or failed to take steps to prevent it or report it to the authorities. The accountability will also be extended to non-state superiors in relevant cases, the draft said.
The law allowed the victims or witnesses to file lawsuit with the police and in case of any refusal by police the victim can go directly to the court to lodge the complaint.
Investigations must generally be completed within 90 days. Trials of those cases will be held in the court of Sessions Judges and expected to be completed within 90 working days.
The law allows a spouse or children to apply to the court to use or transfer of the property of the missing person in their names to cover essential living expenses and debts.
If a person is missing for five years, a "Disappearance Certificate" can be issued to settle inheritance matters.
The government will maintain a national database of the disappeared persons and establish a Compensation and Rehabilitation Fund for victims and their families.
The draft specifies that the cases involving widespread or systematic disappearances will be tried under the International Crimes (Tribunals) Act, 1973.
Any misuse of the law will make a person responsible for up to five years imprisonment, the draft proposed.

item.title: BMD: Rainfall likely to continue over next five days
item.description:
Monsoon remains fairly active over Bangladesh as a low-pressure area forms over the Northwest BayThe Bangladesh Meteorological Department (BMD) has forecast that rainfall is likely to continue across the country over the next five days from 9am on Saturday, as the monsoon remains fairly active over Bangladesh.
“Light to moderate rain or thundershowers, accompanied by temporary gusty winds, are likely to occur at many places over Rangpur, Mymensingh, Chittagong and Sylhet divisions and at a few places over Rajshahi, Dhaka, Khulna and Barisal divisions, with moderately heavy falls at places across the country,” said a regular bulletin of the Met office.
Day and night temperatures may remain nearly unchanged across the country.
A low-pressure area has formed over the Northwest Bay and adjoining West Bengal-North Odisha coasts. It is likely to move west-northwestwards.
The axis of the monsoon trough runs through Rajasthan, Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, with one end extending to Assam across the southern part of Bangladesh through the centre of the low-pressure area.
The monsoon is fairly active over Bangladesh and strong over the North Bay.

item.title: India says Ganga treaty issues to be discussed under JRC
item.description:
India has said issues relating to the Ganga Water Treaty between Bangladesh and India will be discussed under the framework of the bilateral Joint Rivers Commission (JRC) as Bangladesh awaits New Delhi’s response on the matter.
“Ganga Water Treaty was signed in 1996 for a period of 30 years and all water related issues, river related issues between India and Bangladesh are discussed as part of the agenda of the bilateral Joint Rivers Commission,” said Official Spokesperson at the Indian Ministry of External Affairs Randhir Jaiswal.
Talking to reporters in New Delhi recently, Jaiswal said further meetings of the Joint Committee of the Ganga Water Treaty continue to be held at the technical level.
The government is determined to renegotiate the Ganga Water Sharing Treaty with India while preserving the rights of the Bangladeshi people.
Replying to a supplementary question from Bagerhat-4 lawmaker Md Abdul Aleem, Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur Rahman on Thursday said Bangladesh remains active in pursuing its fair share of water from common rivers.
He said a team has been formed to prepare a new agreement following the expiry of the Ganges Water-sharing Treaty, and the Indian authorities have been informed accordingly. “We are now waiting for their response.”
The Bangladesh-India Ganga/Ganges Water Treaty was signed in 1996 for a period of 30 years which is expiring in December this year.
Experts said the treaty needs to be “reviewed and reformed comprehensively” before going for a renewed treaty by engaging economists, urban planners, sociologists and environmentalists in the planning, as Dhaka shares the ‘risk’ of not sharing it appropriately.
Foreign Minister Dr Khalilur, while attending the ninth Indian Ocean Conference in Mauritius, said they would like to see that there is an arrangement and a new treaty, or a revised treaty, ensuring the essential needs of their people.
“These are common rivers, and we have common legacies here, common interests and, as I said, there's no other alternative but to seek a solution that is durable and will win public trust. And this will also be very important to lay the basis for the relationship over the next 25 to 50 years,” he told NDTV on the sidelines of the conference.
“I think it is very important for Bangladesh and India to renew the Ganges Treaty. But it has to be revised. The very simple reason is that the treaty was done almost three decades ago,” Prof Shahab Enam Khan, who is the Executive Director of Bangladesh Center for Indo-Pacific Affairs, told recently.

item.title: Agriculture minister: No shortage of fertilizer, action if artificial crisis created
item.description:
Agriculture and Fisheries and Livestock Minister Mohammed Aminur Rashid on Saturday said the country has sufficient fertiliser supplies and warned that strict action would be taken against anyone found creating an artificial shortage or charging farmers excessive prices.
He made the remarks at a meeting with government officials at the deputy commissioner’s office in Faridpur.
Faridpur Deputy Commissioner Mazharul Islam presided over the meeting.
The minister said the country imports 1.5 million tonnes more fertiliser than its total demand, leaving no scope for a shortage.
He said some fertilizer retailers are spreading rumours that fertiliser is unavailable in the market while supplying it when offered extra money.
The minister said the government is farmer-friendly and will do whatever is necessary for the development of farmers.“The government believes that the country will progress if farmers prosper.”
He said the quality of soil in the country has deteriorated for various reasons, but Faridpur’s soil is still among the best in the country.
Such fertile soil is difficult to find in many other districts, creating significant opportunities to further develop agriculture in Faridpur, he added.
The minister said the government is working to stop imports of jute and onion seeds in the future.
He said another major government target in agriculture is to reduce imports of agricultural products and meet domestic demand through increased local production.
“Our main target is to ensure that we do not have to import any agricultural products in the future. We are trying to produce them ourselves. Everyone concerned will have to work hard and make efforts to achieve this,” he said.
He instructed dealers to play a responsible role in ensuring that fertiliser reaches farmers on time and at fair prices.
Director General of the Department of Agricultural Extension Mohammad Abdur Rahim, Faridpur, Additional Superintendent of Police Fatema Islam, Additional Deputy Commissioner Sohrab Hossain and Deputy Director of the Department of Agricultural Extension agriculturist Shahaduzzaman, among others, attended the meeting.

item.title: 17 banks pledge Tk17,000cr to revive closed factories
item.description:
Seventeen commercial banks have joined hands with Bangladesh Bank to fund a Tk41,000 crore credit pool aimed at restarting long-shuttered industrial plants, driving private investment, and lifting the economy out of its recent slump.
The commitment forms the backbone of a broader Tk60,000 crore stimulus package first unveiled by the central bank on May 23.
Under the agreement, participating commercial lenders will cover Tk41,000 crore of the total allocation, while Bangladesh Bank will finance the remaining Tk19,000 crore directly from its internal reserves.
The participating institutions include a mix of state-owned and leading private lenders: Sonali Bank, Agrani Bank, Rupali Bank, Brac Bank, City Bank, Jamuna Bank, Dutch-Bangla Bank, Mutual Trust Bank, Uttara Bank, Prime Bank, Bank Asia, NCC Bank, Pubali Bank, Eastern Bank, Mercantile Bank, Trust Bank, and Southeast Bank.
At the heart of the initiative is a dedicated Tk20,000 crore allotment—the package's largest single component—specifically targeted at getting dormant factories back into operation.
Private entrepreneurs will be eligible to tap into these funds via loans carrying an average interest rate of 7.5%.
Terming the scheme a core "Production and Employment Recovery" program, Bangladesh Bank Governor Md Mostakur Rahman noted during a recent press briefing that the central bank expects the initiative to generate nearly 2.5 million new jobs.
Beyond immediate employment, financial regulators anticipate that restoring closed production lines will catalyze broader private sector investment and supply the momentum needed to break the economy's ongoing stagnation.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 963 as three die in 24 hours
item.description:
Three more children have died from measles-like symptoms in the 24 hours leading up to 8:00am on Saturday, raising the overall death toll from the ongoing outbreak to 963.
With the latest figures, the total number of suspected measles deaths has reached 864, while the number of confirmed deaths remained unchanged at 99, as no new confirmed measles deaths were reported in the last 24 hours.
The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) has classified all three of the latest casualties as suspected.
Among the three new suspected fatalities, the highest concentration was recorded in Dhaka, with two deaths reported in both the Dhaka division and Dhaka district.
A total of 886 suspected measles cases were recorded in the 24 hours till Saturday morning, taking the overall suspected case tally to 155,678.
During the same period, 57 new confirmed measles cases were reported, bringing the total number of confirmed infections to 18,853.
Since March 15, 2026, a total of 136,257 suspected measles patients have been hospitalized across the country, of whom 131,264 have recovered and been discharged from hospitals, according to the DGHS.

item.title: Headteacher dies after falling from rickshaw during mugging near parliament
item.description:
A primary school head teacher died after falling from a rickshaw when two muggers allegedly snatched her bag near the South Plaza of the National Parliament building in Dhaka on Saturday morning.
The incident occurred around 6:30am at the South Plaza.
The deceased was identified as Ranjina Parvin, head teacher of Bagbari Girls’ Government Primary School in Bogra.
According to information available, Ranjina had travelled from Bogra overnight to see a doctor at Islamia Eye Hospital in Farmgate. She got off at Gabtoli bus terminal at dawn and then took a rickshaw towards the hospital.
When the rickshaw reached the South Plaza of the Parliament building, the muggers allegedly approached from behind on a motorcycle and snatched her bag. She fell from the rickshaw and sustained a head injury.
She was rescued from the scene and taken to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital where the doctor on duty declared her dead.
Tejgaon Division Deputy Commissioner (DC) Ibne Mizan said police were working to identify the motorcycle and those involved.
He expressed hope that the suspects would be identified and arrested within a short time.

item.title: Nepal-China flood: Death toll reaches 633, missing near 3,000
item.description:
Rescuers in Nepal and China were battling Saturday to locate thousands of people missing days after a deadly, tsunami-like wall of water and debris swept through the Himalayan region, engulfing entire villages.
The latest figures from both countries put the number of missing close to 3,000, with 633 bodies recovered -- and reports of some dead possibly swept downstream as far away as India.
Rescue worker Kawan Koirala, from the Nepal Scout Disaster Response Team, said they were struggling in thick, leg-sucking mud.
“People want their family’s body back, either dead or alive, but we cannot find them... you can see the mud,” he told AFP, exhausted after an 18-hour shift.
“It is very traumatic for me too. It is my first time seeing these types of things. Everywhere is mud. We faced floods in Nepal before, but not like this.”
The US Geological Survey said the disaster on Wednesday on the Tibet-Nepal border was caused by a glacial collapse that created a torrent of debris downstream.
Survivors face an agonizing wait to learn the fate of missing relatives, and the prospect of rebuilding their lives from nothing.
“All the settlements near the river were swept away,” Buddhi Ram Dangol told AFP in Nepal’s Nuwakot district. “There is nothing left.”
At Bidur’s army base, a key rescue hub in the same district, relatives crowded around lists of rescued people pasted on a wall.
“I have come here looking for my son,” said Kalka Sharda, scanning the list in desperation. “He was a laborer at the hydropower plant, but I can’t find his name, and the authorities are not saying anything.”
In an area home to vast energy infrastructure projects, Nepal’s disaster authority listed 933 hydropower workers among the missing, along with 517 foreigners, including trekkers and pilgrims to Tibet’s sacred Mount Kailash.
The trauma of Wednesday’s catastrophe has been “enormous,” and as many as 93,000 people may have been affected, the Red Cross said, with the death toll expected to rise.
Emergency teams worked flat out to find survivors as widespread devastation left communities short of food and water.
Fears of further flooding have compounded the search for the missing.
The deluge of ice and mud caused huge lakes, and one of these formations has become a risk of further floods.
While the exact cause of the collapse is unclear, climate change is causing glaciers to melt worldwide, increasing the risks of such disasters.
In Tibet, where Chinese authorities are the only source of information, Beijing had paused its rescue operation at the hardest-hit area of Gyirong over the risk of renewed flooding.
On the Nepali side, soldiers were trying desperately to drill through to 100 people trapped in the tunnel of the Trishuli 3A hydropower project on Saturday.
The prime minister’s office said teams had begun “clearing mud and debris” to open the entrance, while a specialized Indian tunnel rescue unit had arrived to help.
Workers rescued from other dam projects along the Trishuli valley described a disaster that unfolded with terrifying speed.
Nepal reported a death toll of 626 people on Saturday.
There are 2,426 people, including hundreds of foreigners, who are out of contact in the country.
Across the border in Tibet, which is largely inaccessible to foreign journalists, seven people died and 554 remain missing, the state Xinhua news agency said Saturday.
Authorities also said they had evacuated 555 stranded tourists and 499 Chinese residents from Tibet.
In India, authorities said they had recovered seven bodies from rivers flowing from Nepal, believed to be flood victims.
Scores of Hindu devotees from across the world are among those missing on the border, as many were on a pilgrimage to Tibet’s Mount Kailash.
Sivaranjani Muthunathan was travelling by bus with 56 others towards the Chinese border when they became stuck in what they thought was a traffic jam.
“Then there was fog, smoke, something that seemed to suddenly engulf us,” Muthunathan, 46, told AFP on Friday, showing a phone video she recorded of a torrent surging towards her.
Around them, vehicles were swept away or buried under mud.
“One by one, we also climbed out through the driver’s side,” then scrambled up a hill, she said.

item.title: PM Tarique hands job appointment letters to families of movement victims
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Saturday handed over job appointment letters to family members of those who were subjected to enforced disappearance or killed during the movement against the Awami League government, as well as families of those killed in the July mass uprising.
The appointment letters were handed over at an event held at the Karabi Hall of the Prime Minister’s Tejgaon Office in Dhaka around noon.
Family members of the victims and officials from various levels of the government attended the event.
Several recipients became emotional after receiving their appointment letters. The prime minister assured them that he would always stand by them.
The program was conducted by the Prime Minister’s Additional Press Secretary Atikur Rahman Rumon.

item.title: Law minister: Govt to decide on Makkah Pact after considering all aspects
item.description:
Law, Justice and Parliamentary Affairs Minister Md Asaduzzaman has said the government will decide whether Bangladesh will join the Makkah Pact after considering all aspects of the matter.
He made the remarks on Saturday while responding to questions from journalists after attending a reception for meritorious students of Jhenidah Collectorate School and College as the chief guest.
Deputy Commissioner Md Noman Hossain presided over the program, while Prime Minister’s Political Assistant Rashed Khan attended as the special guest.
The law minister said India would act according to its foreign policy, while Bangladesh would follow its own policy.
“India will move like India, and Bangladesh will move like Bangladesh,” he added.
Regarding the country’s law and order situation, Asaduzzaman said the issue was not whether the government was satisfied with the situation, but whether it was making relentless efforts to maintain normalcy.
He said the government and the Ministry of Law are also working to introduce e-judiciary to digitalize the country’s judicial system.
The government plans to implement the e-judiciary system within the next year, he added.
District BNP President MA Majid, General Secretary Zahiduzzaman Mona, Vice-President Munshi Kamal Azad Pannu, Joint General Secretary Abdul Majid Biswas and Shailkupa upazila BNP General Secretary Humayun Babar Firoz, among other BNP leaders and activists of its affiliated organizations, attended the reception.

item.title: Zimbabwe crash involving church minibus kills 27
item.description:
A minibus carrying churchgoers collided head-on with a truck in central Zimbabwe, killing at least 27 people, police said Saturday, in the latest deadly road crash to hit the country.
The crash occurred at around 1830 GMT on Friday near Chivhu, about 140 kilometres (87 miles) south of the capital Harare, police said.
The foreign-registered haulage truck was overtaking another vehicle when it collided with the minibus, which was carrying worshippers to a conference.
Both vehicles were carrying an “unknown” number of passengers, police said. Seven people were injured in the crash.
Footage shared on social media by public broadcaster ZBC showed the mangled minibus charred to a shell, with the truck coming to rest on the opposite side of the road.
The crash occurred in a flat, remote stretch of road, with low vegetation lining the roadside and open terrain beyond.
Traffic accidents are common in Zimbabwe, where roads are riddled with potholes due to years of underfunding and neglect, and driving standards can be poor.
For everyday transport, many Zimbabweans rely on the privately run minibus taxis, known locally as kombi, but they are often criticized for overloading.
In April, at least 18 people were killed when a minibus burst into flames on a highway in the south, while earlier that month a woman and her five children died when their vehicle collided with a haulage truck on another highway linking Zimbabwe and South Africa.

item.title: At least 27 dead after Russian strike on warehouse near Kyiv
item.description:
At least 27 people have died after a Russian drone struck a warehouse near Kyiv’s western suburbs overnight, sparking a huge fire and explosions, authorities said Saturday.
The warehouse appeared to have been storing “explosive objects,” Ukrainian prosecutors said, opening an investigation into criminal negligence.
Officials did not give details about the nature of the facility.
Both Russia and Ukraine have intensified long-range strikes on each other in recent months, sparking fires and sending civilian casualties to record levels.
AFP reporters saw a huge column of black smoke pouring over the capital’s western suburbs, as officials reported the facility was still on fire.
“Unfortunately, as things stand, 27 people are known to have died. And this figure may not be final,” Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko said.
Among the dead was Taras Didych, mayor of the village of Dmytrivska, he added.
Ukrainian prosecutors announced an investigation.
“On 28 August at around 8:10pm (1710 GMT), an unmanned aerial vehicle... fell on or struck the grounds of an enterprise in the town of Myla,” the office of Ukraine’s prosecutor general said.
Myla is a town on Kyiv’s western outskirts.
“A large-scale fire broke out on the enterprise’s grounds, and detonation began,” it added.
The prosecutor’s office specified that its investigation would focus on “the legality of the... storage of explosive objects and materials on the enterprise’s grounds,” as well as whether the company, which was not named, had the “necessary permits and approvals.’
Prime Minister Sergiy Koretsky expressed regret that a “lesson” had not been learned after a previous deadly attack in July in Vyshneve, near Kyiv, on a munitions depot.
That investigation revealed serious failings on the part of the state-owned company, which did not comply with standards despite the proximity of residential buildings.
“In the fifth year of the full-scale invasion, making the same mistakes over and over is criminal negligence,” he said on Telegram.
“Everyone responsible, without exception, must face severe punishment so that such situations never happen again.”

Gold price drops by Tk7,109 per bhori
item.description:
The price of 22-carat gold has been reduced by Tk7,109 per bhori in Bangladesh, with the new rate coming into effect from 10am on Saturday, according to the Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus).
Under the new rate, 22-carat gold will cost Tk20,630 per gram, or Tk240,636 per bhori (11.664 grams), including VAT. The previous price was Tk247,745 per bhori.
The decision was taken at a meeting of Bajus's Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring on Saturday morning, following a decline in the price of Tejabi gold (pure gold) and silver in the local market.
According to the new rates, 21-carat gold has been priced at Tk19,700 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,920 per gram. Gold under the traditional system has been set at Tk13,820 per gram.
On a per-bhori basis, 21-carat gold will cost approximately Tk229,891, 18-carat gold Tk197,333 and traditional-system gold approximately Tk161,173.
Bajus has also reduced the price of silver.
The new price of 22-carat silver has been set at Tk455 per gram, 21-carat at Tk435, 18-carat at Tk375 and traditional-system silver at Tk285 per gram.
The previous price of 22-carat silver was Tk470 per gram, meaning it has fallen by Tk15 per gram.
On Tuesday, Bajus had set the price of 22-carat gold at Tk21,240 per gram, or Tk247,745 per bhori.
At the time, 21-carat gold was priced at Tk20,285 per gram, 18-carat at Tk17,420 and traditional-system gold at Tk14,225 per gram.
Bajus had also raised gold prices on August 22. The latest reduction comes after several changes in gold prices in the final week of August.
Bajus said VAT is included in the announced selling prices, so customers cannot be charged VAT separately. However, making charges will be added depending on the design of the jewellery.
The association also said its existing rules will remain in effect for the exchange, purchase and sale of gold and silver jewellery, excluding VAT, making charges and the value of stones.
The new prices will remain effective at all jewellery shops across the country until further notice from Bajus.

Chief justice warns against use of AI in court judgments
item.description:
Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury has warned that artificial intelligence (AI) must not be used to write court judgments.
He made the remarks while inaugurating the country’s first AI Governance Summer School at the Asiatic Society Bangladesh auditorium in Dhaka on Saturday.
The chief justice said AI cannot be used to assess the subject matter of cases, relevant laws and provisions, facts and evidence, or a judge’s conscience. He therefore urged caution in using AI in judicial decision-making.
He also called for effective laws and policies to determine where and to what extent AI can be used.
“AI must be used to make people’s lives easier and protect fundamental rights,” he said.
The chief justice said training and skills were more important than infrastructure in ensuring the effective use of AI.
He also warned that using information generated by AI without proper verification could be risky.

item.title: Traffic movement returns to normal on Dhaka-Chittagong highway
item.description:
Traffic movement on the Dhaka-Chittagong highway has returned to normal after a covered van broke down in the Narayanganj section, causing a traffic jam stretching about 1km.
The congestion occurred on the Chittagong-bound lane in the Pirojpur Union area on Saturday morning. Highway police later removed the vehicle, restoring normal traffic flow.
According to highway police and local sources, a large pothole developed on the Dhaka-bound section of the highway in the Ashari Char area following recent heavy rain. Urgent repair work was subsequently undertaken.
A pothole measuring about five metres wide was filled with micro-concrete, forcing authorities to close one lane from Friday morning until Saturday morning. The lane was reopened after the repair work was completed.
Meanwhile, the covered van broke down on the Chittagong-bound lane in the Pirojpur Union area on Saturday morning, causing congestion for about 1km. The traffic jam extended to the Meghna Toll Plaza.
Upon receiving the information, highway police removed the vehicle and traffic movement returned to normal.
Rubel Hossain, a passenger from Sonargaon’s Mograpara area, said: “There is no traffic jam here now. A covered van broke down in the Pirojpur Union area of the highway, causing congestion.”
Kachpur Highway Police Station Officer-in-Charge Shamim Sheikh confirmed the matter, saying a temporary traffic jam occurred after the covered van broke down.
“Upon receiving the information, highway police removed the vehicle. Traffic movement has now returned to normal,” he said.
The OC also said one lane near the Ashari Char Bridge was closed on Friday for repair work but was reopened on Saturday morning after the work was completed.

item.title: Home minister announces Tk2 L reward for information on looted, illegal arms
item.description:
Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed has announced a cash reward of up to Tk200,000 for information leading to the recovery of looted and illegal weapons.
He also warned that police officers who fail to make progress within set deadlines in controlling terrorism, extortion and drugs will face strict legal and administrative action.
The minister made the remarks while briefing journalists on Saturday following a “Quarterly Crime Review Meeting” at the Rajarbagh Police Auditorium.
Salahuddin said police would undertake targeted efforts to recover looted and illegal weapons, with a special police unit being formed for the purpose.
To encourage people to assist in recovering the weapons, the government has announced rewards of up to Tk200,000, he said.
At the meeting, police members raised various issues concerning law and order, including the need for increased technological support in their work.
The home minister said the government was working on these matters and issued necessary directives to maintain the law-and-order situation.
Responding to journalists’ questions after the meeting, he said police had been instructed that the law-and-order situation would gradually improve further.

item.title: Justice Habibul Gani to take oath as Appellate Division judge Sunday
item.description:
Newly appointed Appellate Division judge Justice Md Habibul Gani will take oath at 9:30am on Sunday, with Chief Justice Zubayer Rahman Chowdhury scheduled to administer the oath.
The Supreme Court’s Public Relations Officer Md Shafiqul Islam said this in a notice issued on Saturday.
President appointed Justice Md Habibul Gani, a judge of the High Court Division, to the Appellate Division on Thursday. A gazette notification was subsequently issued on his appointment.
Justice Habibul Gani has served in the High Court Division since 2011. His orders and judgments in several important cases have included a case concerning the Dhaka University Central Students’ Union (Ducsu) election.
With his appointment, the Appellate Division now has five judges, including the chief justice.

item.title: Irene Khan assumes charge as Bangladesh’s permanent representative to UN
item.description:
Internationally renowned human rights expert Irene Zubaida Khan has assumed office as Bangladesh’s new permanent representative to the United Nations.
Irene Khan formally took charge on Friday by presenting her credentials to UN Secretary-General António Guterres at the UN Headquarters in New York.
With decades of international experience, Irene has worked extensively on human rights, international law, refugee protection, the rule of law and sustainable development. Throughout her career, she has held senior positions at the United Nations and other international organisations.
Since 2020, she has served as the UN Special Rapporteur on the promotion and protection of the right to freedom of opinion and expression.
Earlier, Irene served as Secretary General of Amnesty International from 2001 to 2009, becoming the first woman to lead the organisation.
From 2012 to 2019, she served as Director-General of the International Development Law Organization (IDLO).
Before that, she spent 21 years with the Office of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), where she held several senior positions, including Chief of Mission in India and Deputy Director of the Division of International Protection.
In recognition of her contributions to human rights and peace, Khan received the prestigious Sydney Peace Prize in 2006.
She is also the author of The Unheard Truth: Poverty and Human Rights.
Irene studied law at the University of Manchester and Harvard Law School.

item.title: ‘Public awareness rally’ in Gulshan demands action against illegal auto-rickshaws
item.description:
Residents of Gulshan, Banani, Baridhara and Niketan have made five demands, including action against illegal auto-rickshaws, easing traffic congestion and ensuring safe alternative public transport.
They made the demands at a public awareness rally organized by the Gulshan Society at Gulshan-2 on Friday afternoon.
Gulshan Society President Barrister Omar Sadat, the rally’s chief organizer, said: “We are not against auto-rickshaws or anyone’s livelihood. We want safe roads. To achieve this, all types of vehicles must operate in an orderly and regulated manner.”
He said: “A country cannot run by relying on rickshaws. There is no such system anywhere in the world. Therefore, illegal auto-rickshaws must be removed and alternative livelihood opportunities must be created for their drivers. Necessary training should also be arranged for them.”
Omar Sadat said uncontrolled transport and severe traffic congestion were among the country’s major problems.
“One of the problems of our country is unbearable traffic congestion and an uncontrolled transport system. To move the economy forward, we need a skilled workforce, which we lack. This is why foreign investment is not coming,” he said.
“We have been talking for a long time about illegal battery-powered rickshaws and the congestion, disorder and insecurity they cause. But the problem has not been resolved,” he added.
He expressed determination to continue the protest until the demands are met.
The five demands are: allowing only licensed auto-rickshaws to operate; restricting their movement on major, important and high-risk roads; ensuring regular enforcement of traffic laws; introducing safe alternative public transport; and providing alternative livelihood opportunities for auto-rickshaw drivers.
Gulshan Society Secretary General Mujibur Rahman Mridha, former Secretary General Barrister Sarwat Siraj Shukla, Banani Society President Shawkat Ali Dilan and other prominent residents of the areas attended the rally and spoke in support of the demands.

item.title: 5,000 underprivileged people receive free eye care in Bogra
item.description:
Nearly 5,000 underprivileged people in Bogra received free eye treatment and healthcare services at a medical camp held at Bogra Poura High School and College on Friday.
The camp was organized by Al-Bashar International Foundation with support from the Ziaur Rahman Foundation, at the initiative of Dr Zubaida Rahman, Vice President of the Ziaur Rahman Foundation and a cardiologist.
Women, men and children from different parts of the district attended the camp, where they received free eye examinations, medical consultations and necessary healthcare services. Doctors also provided medicines and eyeglasses to patients based on their medical needs.
Cataract patients were identified during the camp, and arrangements were made for free surgery in cases requiring further treatment. As part of the initiative, 500 patients have been selected to undergo cataract surgery with intraocular lenses free of charge at the 250-bed Mohammad Ali Hospital in Bogra.
Former MP Helaluzzaman Talukder Lalu, vice-president of the Jatiyatabadi Krishak Dal, visited the camp. He inspected the activities, spoke with doctors and patients, and distributed medicines and eyeglasses among the beneficiaries.
Among others, Al-Bashar International Foundation Bangladesh Sector Country Director Dr Ahmed Taher Hamid Ali, BNP Central Committee member Ali Azgar Talukder Hena, Bogra district BNP leaders Fazlul Bari Talukder Belal and M R Islam Swadhin, and representatives of the Ziaur Rahman Foundation and Al Noor Eye Hospital were present.
Organizers said many low-income people cannot receive timely eye treatment due to financial constraints. The initiative was aimed at bringing essential eye care, particularly treatment for cataracts and vision problems, to those who cannot afford it.
They said such humanitarian and healthcare programs would continue in the future as part of efforts to support disadvantaged communities.

item.title: Neighbor sent to jail over alleged rape of six-year-old
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Friday sent Sumon Mia, a neighbor to jail over the alleged rape of a six-year-old child in Dhaka’s Shah Ali police station area.
Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ismail passed the order following an application by the investigation officer in the case.
Shah Ali Police Station Sub-Inspector (SI) Osman Gani, the investigation officer, produced Sumon before the court and sought an order to keep him in jail.
Sub-Inspector Ila Moni of the prosecution department said there was no bail application on behalf of the accused. The court subsequently ordered him to be sent to jail.
Police arrested Sumon from a residence near the Shah Ali Royal City Pocket Gate at around 8pm on Thursday.
Niaz Mehedi, additional deputy commissioner of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Media and Public Relations Division, citing police and the police station, said: “A complaint was received that the child had been raped in the area at around 4:30pm on Wednesday.”
“Later, the child’s mother took her to Shaheed Suhrawardy Medical College Hospital. After examination, doctors suspected that the child might have been raped. She was then referred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital for advanced treatment.”
Niaz Mehedi further said: “When the child’s mother asked her, she mentioned Sumon, a tenant in the neighboring house.”
“The child alleged that Suman took her to his room and raped her.”
The child’s mother filed a case at Shah Ali Police Station on Thursday in connection with the incident.

item.title: Kamrangirchar Loha Bridge reopens after 25-day renovation
item.description:
Dhaka South City Corporation (DSCC) has reopened the Kamrangirchar Loha Bridge after completing renovation work in 25 days with its own funding.
DSCC Administrator and freedom fighter Md Abdus Salam inaugurated the renovated bridge on Friday, with Dhaka-7 MP Hamidur Rahman attending as the special guest.
The 145-metre-long and 4.2-metre-wide bridge is used by around 70,000 people every day. The renovation is expected to benefit nearly 5 million residents of Kamrangirchar.
The renovation of the dilapidated bridge is expected to ease travel difficulties for local residents and pedestrians while improving safety.
Speaking at the inauguration, DSCC Administrator Md Abdus Salam said the city corporation was committed to making travel easier and safer for city residents.
He said completing the renovation in a record 25 days with DSCC’s own funding demonstrated that commitment.
Salam said an initiative had also been taken to revise the proposed eight-lane project to preserve the historic bridge for future generations.
He announced that the bridge would henceforth be open only to pedestrians.
DSCC Region-3 Executive Engineer Ahsan Habib, officials concerned and local dignitaries were present at the inauguration.

item.title: Putin congratulates President Mirza Fakhrul
item.description:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has congratulated newly elected Bangladesh President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir, wishing him success in serving the people of Bangladesh.
In a congratulatory message, the Russian president extended his best wishes to his Bangladeshi counterpart on his election as President of the People's Republic of Bangladesh, said the Russian embassy in Dhaka.
Putin wished President Mirza Fakhrul well-being, sound health and success in his future endeavors for the benefit of the friendly people of Bangladesh.

item.title: Dhaka-Mawa Expressway sees 548 accidents since Padma Bridge opening
item.description:
A total of 548 road accidents have occurred on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway since the Padma Bridge was opened on June 25, 2022, leaving 147 people dead and 874 injured, according to fire service sources.
Muhammad Shafiqul Islam, deputy assistant director of Munshiganj Fire Service and Civil Defense, said the accidents occurred between the Mawa Toll Plaza and Dhaleshwari Toll Plaza of the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway.
He said that from June 25, 2022 to Thursday, August 27, 2026, a total of 548 road accidents were recorded on the stretch.
Fire service firefighters risked their lives to rescue the injured and send them to hospitals, Shafiqul said. They also recovered the bodies of those killed and handed them over to police.
He said the number of road accidents is increasing alongside growing vehicle pressure on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway.
In this situation, drivers and the general public need to become more aware to prevent accidents, he said.
Shafiqul also urged drivers to refrain from risky overtaking, follow road instructions and traffic signals properly, and drive within the prescribed speed limit.
He added that drivers should obey traffic laws, maintain a safe distance and refrain from inattentive and reckless driving to help reduce road accidents on the Dhaka-Mawa Expressway.

item.title: High paddy seedling prices put farmers in distress
item.description:
Farmers in Sonatala upazila of Bogra are facing growing difficulties as the prices of Aman paddy seedlings have surged in local markets, despite ample supplies. They have urged the authorities to take immediate steps to keep paddy seedling prices within an affordable range.
During visits to several markets, including Syed Ahmed College Haat, Karamja Haat, Thakurpara Sanyasi Mela Haat, Velurpara Haat, Karpur Haat, Balua Haat, Harikhali Haat, Tekani Chukainagar Haat and Pakulla Haat, large quantities of paddy seedlings were found being brought in for sale.
Seedlings of BRRI Dhan-28, 29, 89 and 92, as well as Ranjit and various local varieties, were available. Eighty bundles were selling for Tk 350 to Tk 400. Seedlings of aromatic white- and black-grain varieties were considerably more expensive, with 80 bundles priced at Tk 700 to Tk 800.
Farmers said many of their own paddy seedlings had been damaged by prolonged dry weather, excessive heat, inadequate rainfall and irrigation shortages. As a result, they have been forced to depend on market-bought seedlings for Aman cultivation.
They also alleged that some traders and seedling producers were exploiting the increased demand to charge higher prices. According to farmers, the prices of paddy seedlings have risen nearly two to three times compared with last year.
Abdul Alim, a farmer from Padmapara village, said his seedbed dried up despite repeated irrigation efforts. “I could not save my seedlings despite providing irrigation and trying to protect them from the intense heat. I had no option but to come to the market, but the prices are too high,” he said.
Farmers Rafiqul Islam, Mozammel Haque and Bokul Pramanik of Thakurpara said rising diesel and irrigation costs had increased seedling production expenses. They added that paddy seedlings had also been damaged in some low-lying areas after fields were inundated.
Sonatala Upazila Agriculture Officer Krishibid Sohrab Hossain said the agriculture office was providing farmers with necessary technical advice to ensure successful Aman cultivation in line with the production target.
“Market monitoring is being strengthened to prevent paddy seedling shortages and ensure the sale of quality seedlings at reasonable prices,” he said.

item.title: King Harald, ‘symbol’ of Norway, dead at 89
item.description:
Norway’s King Harald has died aged 89, the palace said on Friday, his 53-year-old son Crown Prince Haakon automatically succeeding him on the throne.
Haakon takes over a monarchy long hailed for its modernity and modesty, but beset by a string of scandals in recent years.
“It is with deep sadness that we announce that His Majesty King Harald passed away today. King Harald passed away peacefully at Oslo University Hospital on Friday, August 28 at 6:35am,” (0435 GMT) it said in a statement.
The flag at the royal palace in Oslo was lowered to half-mast, as crowds gathered outside the palace to pay their respects.
Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Store said he had received the news with “deep sorrow.”
“An entire nation mourns, and at the same time remains profoundly grateful for a long life devoted to Norway,” he said in a statement.
“King Harald loved Norway. And Norway loved its king.”
The government later announced a period of national mourning until the king was buried.
Hundreds of flowers had already been laid outside the palace the day before, after it announced the king was in “extremely serious” condition in hospital.
Vigdis Haug, 65, said she valued Harald’s ability to unify people.
“I think he has been such a down-to-earth king who has cared about all of us, and the words he always uses when he gives a speech are so wise and so valuable,” she told AFP.
Haug and others to whom AFP spoke pointed in particular to Harald’s speech after the neo-Nazi Anders Behring Breivik killed 77 people in twin attacks on July 22, 2011, in Norway’s worst massacre since World War II.
“He was someone who always seemed to find the words that brought us together and gave us a sense of security,” Caroline Vagle, a reporter for magazine Se og Hor, told AFP.
Neighboring Sweden’s King Carl XVI Gustaf called him “an outstanding representative of his country. He gave ‘All for Norway,’” referring to Harald’s royal motto.
Denmark’s King Frederik meanwhile called the late monarch “an extraordinary man.”
Britain’s King Charles III said he mourned the death of his “dear cousin,” hailing Harald as a “towering figure.”
Harald was king when the Oslo Accords between Israel and the Palestine Liberation Organization (PLO) were negotiated in the 1990s, and Israeli President Isaac Herzog said he was “deeply saddened” by his passing.
Church bells were to ring across Norway at noon (1000 GMT) to mark the king’s passing.
Haakon was to meet with the government on Friday to formally inform it of the monarch’s death, and to announce the royal name and motto he has chosen.
After that, the flag over the royal palace will be raised to the top again, while another flag on the royal balcony and at other official buildings will remain at half-mast until after Harald’s funeral.
Haakon’s 22-year-old daughter Ingrid Alexandra also automatically becomes crown princess.
Europe’s oldest reigning monarch, King Harald had been in hospital in Oslo since August 17, suffering from haemolytic anaemia, a condition caused by an abnormally rapid destruction of red blood cells which leads to fatigue and shortness of breath.
Harald, who ascended the Norwegian throne in 1991, embodied an open and tolerant Norway during his reign.
He faced mounting health problems in his final years, forcing him to scale back his official schedule.
But he always ruled out abdicating, arguing that he took a lifelong oath before the Norwegian parliament.
The past year has been a turbulent one for the Norwegian royal family.
In addition to his own health struggles, his wife Queen Sonja, also 89, was briefly admitted to hospital in May due to heart problems.
Haakon’s wife Mette-Marit is under scrutiny for her ties to the late US sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.
Documents published in January in the United States revealed her sustained and at times intimate correspondence with Epstein between 2011 and 2014, at a time when the American financier had already been convicted.
In June, Mette-Marit’s son from a relationship prior to her marriage to Haakon, Marius Borg Hoiby, was sentenced to four years in prison for two rapes. He has appealed the verdict.
Suffering herself from a serious lung disease, Mette-Marit, 53, had to undergo a lung transplant in July.
The royals remain broadly popular with the Norwegian public, in large part to Harald’s unifying status and his unassuming, modest lifestyle.

Rohingya genocide case: ICJ verdict expected in October
item.description:

He conveyed the expected timeline during a meeting with Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir on the sidelines of the 23rd OIC Extraordinary Council of Foreign Ministers meeting in Jeddah on Thursday.
He noted that the verdict on accountability for the atrocities committed against the Rohingyas would play a critical role in finding a sustainable solution to the Rohingya crisis.
